Two things around the bet ARE supported and should carry the justification instead: (i) committing before the reveal is a pretest/prequestion (g = 0.66, item-specific, requires corrective feedback), and (ii) the confidence value is a feedback-routing signal via hypercorrection. Separately, the scaffolding-removal ladder must be bounded: desirable difficulties reverse with expertise and for high-element-interactivity material, so a top-tier bet on a category where the player holds no component knowledge is a coin flip, not a difficulty.
verdicts_on_design.change: Keep the bet — it is good table dynamics and a legitimate pretest — but stop defending it as a learning intervention and delete the neuroscience and memory-palace rationales. Gate the top tier on per-category component mastery (N prior correct component exposures), greying unearned tiers with an explicit 'unlock by…' line rather than hiding them. Persist `bet_tier` and `was_correct` per attempt and drain a `high_confidence_miss` queue in the session's final round. Keep scoring such that guessing stays attractive — a wrong guess before feedback is productive. Crucially: do NOT let the bet tier also crank distractor confusability; retrieval demand is the difficulty dial, lure plausibility is not.

verdicts_on_design.decision: Decision 2 — 'Items render as the physical object they appear on', with two treatments deliberately hard to read because real ones are.
verdicts_on_design.reasoning: This is the cluster's answer to question (a): YES, the rendering does real work — but on a different mechanism than the design assumed, and the mechanism determines the spec. It is NOT context reinstatement (that effect is small, dies under recognition, and its flagship demonstration failed replication; and the rendering is not environmental context anyway, since it sits inside the stimulus at both study and test). It IS transfer-appropriate processing plus encoding specificity: the effective retrieval cue is the character form AS IT WILL BE MET, so a learner who only ever encodes 出口 as clean black Song on white has encoded a different stimulus from a white-on-green backlit plate. Convergent perceptual support exists — variable-typeface training in a logographic script produced faster responses on NOVEL typefaces at a cost on familiar ones — but it is one single-session study on 24 characters with no delayed test and effects of one-to-two words, so it is a cheap default, not a validated mechanic. A third leg is genuine: the object makes the meaning EVALUABLE, but only through the parts that constrain meaning.
verdicts_on_design.change: Change the rationale in the design doc, because the rationale determines the spec. Fidelity of the SIGN matters a great deal — typeface, stroke weight, spacing, contrast, substrate, and the real colour inversions (white-on-green exit, white-on-red hazard, black-on-yellow price tag). Fidelity of the SURROUNDING SCENE buys nothing and costs retention: no photographic street backgrounds, no atmospheric gradients, no steam off the bowl, no crowd, no perspective warp — those are seductive details, and their effect is strongest under exactly the timed, socially pressured condition this game creates. Drop 'at least three typefaces' as a numeric requirement; the schedule rule is 'do not repeat the substrate this item was last seen on'. Also drop the enforced within-round substrate non-repetition rule — a round of maximally distinct items is a pure list in which distinctiveness effects disappear, and real signage is substrate-homogeneous within a category, so that rule trains against the very percept the TAP argument says to match. On 'deliberately hard to read': acceptable ONLY as fidelity to a genuinely low-contrast real sign, never as a difficulty manipulation — perceptual disfluency is folklore and must be named as banned in the doc.

verdicts_on_design.decision: Decision 3 — 'The component breakdown is the main teaching surface', promoted to the body of the reveal, advanced only by an explicit tap (牛肉 → 牛 + 肉; swap the head for 猪/羊/鸡/鸭肉; then 肉 flattens to 月, giving 肝 肠 肚 腰 脑).
verdicts_on_design.reasoning: The best-supported decision in the product, and the only element with evidence for GENERALISING to unseen items. Explicit semantic-radical instruction transfers to untaught characters in adult CFL learners, and it was demonstrated using precisely a four-option contrastive format holding one component constant and varying the meaning-bearing one — which is exactly the 肉/月 → 肝/肠/肚/腰/脑 move. Morphological awareness is the largest single contributor to L2 Chinese reading, far outranking working-memory capacity. Component decomposition is also what makes a character fit in working memory at all. The 'explicit tap to advance' is right for an independent reason: it keeps reference material off the integration path.
verdicts_on_design.change: Four additions and one prohibition. (1) `transparency` enum per multi-character item (transparent | semi | opaque) — 牛肉 and 出口 branch to a component gloss; 东西 and 麻烦 get an explicit 'this one does not decompose — learn it whole'. Never render a bogus decomposition. (2) Per-component `role` (semantic | phonetic | neither) plus a reliability marker; phonetic components predict pronunciation only ~40% of the time and must never invite meaning inference. (3) Mark every gloss `etymological` or `mnemonic-only` against a scholarly reference — most characters are phono-semantic, so any system supplying a picture-story for every character is fabricating for the majority. (4) Split the schema into `word_decomposition` (morphemes + gloss) and `character_decomposition` (semantic component, phonetic component, transparency of each): 牛肉 = 牛 + 肉 is word-level; 河 = 氵 + 可 is character-level, and one boolean cannot express both. (5) Render the breakdown SPATIALLY inside a square frame (left/right, top/bottom, enclosure) rather than as a linear '出 + 口' string — justified by positional regularity being implicitly acquired by CSL learners, not by neuroimaging. Prohibition: the decomposition unit is components (2–5 per character), never strokes; and no stroke-order animation concurrently with radical markings on the same screen. Sequencing: meet a component inside a whole sign BEFORE naming it (store `component_first_seen_at` per user per component to drive the 'you have seen 肉 before' callback), and reserve the component-contrast card type for items already consolidated.

verdicts_on_design.decision: Decision 4 — 'A confusable is shown beside the target on resolution' (入口 beside 出口, 公斤 beside 斤, 麻 beside 辣).
verdicts_on_design.reasoning: This is the cluster's answer to question (b), and the answer is IT DEPENDS — on four variables that the design must encode, because getting any of them wrong flips the sign of the effect. The resolution PANEL is supported: juxtaposition, not spacing, is the active ingredient in discriminative contrast; temporal separation destroys it; simultaneous paired presentation of visually similar characters improved discrimination in absolute beginners; and interleaving helps precisely the HIGH-similarity categories. What is NOT supported — and is actively risky — is the confusable appearing among the four OPTIONS at test before the sibling is consolidated: plausible lures reliably produce a negative suggestion effect that scales with plausibility, and the mechanism that makes competitive lures beneficial (retrieving why the others are wrong) is unavailable to a learner who does not yet know any of the four. The design decision as written says 'on resolution', which lands on the right side of that line. Note also that the three named pairs are three DIFFERENT problems, and 麻/辣 is the easy one.
verdicts_on_design.change: Encode the four dependencies. (1) WHERE — the pair belongs in the post-resolution panel, and separately, confusable distractors in the four options are gated on the target's `consolidated` bit; first encounters get semantically and visually UNRELATED distractors. (2) WHEN — never introduce both members of a form-confusable pair as new items in the same session; the sibling becomes eligible only once the first is consolidated across a night. (3) WHICH — a `confusion_type` enum with FOUR values, not a boolean: form-confusable (公斤/斤 containment, 人/入) needs staged introduction; meaning-confusable-visually-distinct (麻/辣) can be shown together freely from day one; both; and shared-morpheme (出口/入口, 门口/窗口) — a category no cited study covers, where the shared 口 is a genuine shared meaning that can be TAUGHT, so it plausibly behaves more like the weak semantic case; instrument it. (4) HOW — render both members simultaneously, side by side, same size, same baseline, same neutral ink; do NOT rely on adjacency alone, because learners fail to encode a confusable contrast unless attention is explicitly directed to the critical difference IN WORDS. Every form-confusable pair therefore requires one authored meaning-bearing formula as required content ('出 = feet stepping out of an enclosure; 入 = a wedge entering'). Colour-marking the differing component is an open A/B question tested on delayed discrimination accuracy — neither ship it by default nor prohibit it. Feedback must be corrective and must name the specific lure chosen, and that lure should be recorded so the item's next exposure can re-present the discrimination that actually failed. Finally: enforce pair-balanced testing (RIF ≈ 8.7 points) — a deck that quizzes 出口 and never 入口 is degrading 入口. Prioritise added-stroke pairs early over identical-stroke pairs, which are measurably harder.

verdicts_on_design.decision: Decision 5 — 'Tone colour sits on the pinyin, never on the character.'
verdicts_on_design.reasoning: Supported on the 'never on the character' half, and it costs nothing. Colour and extra visual salience on glyph parts slowed learners in the one Chinese-specific study, and radical markings have separately been found to interfere with L2 character learning; a second visual code on the form competes with the orthographic representation the product exists to build (redundancy effect). The 'tone colour helps' half has no controlled evidence of a learning benefit in either direction — it is a convention, and the palettes are mutually incompatible across apps — so putting it on the pinyin is the right place to park a feature that is decorative rather than load-bearing. Note the accessibility constraint: colour-only tone encoding fails WCAG 1.4.1 and standard four-tone palettes lean on red/green.
verdicts_on_design.change: Keep the rule and state its scope honestly: 'colour never touches the glyph' is the load-bearing half and it generalises — no tinting, highlighting or outlining of any part of a hanzi on the timed card. 'Tone colour on pinyin' is a convention with no learning evidence; do not defend it pedagogically and do not let it grow into a tone-drilling subsystem, which would import the phonological-difficulty gradient into a game that currently escapes it. If tone ever needs a real channel, the evidenced form is multi-talker high-variability phonetic training with immediate feedback, not colour. Do not extend the no-colour rule to a blanket ban on marking the discriminating component in the resolution panel — that ban rests on an RT main effect in one unread study and runs against a meta-analytically supported signalling principle; make it an A/B instead.

directives.directive: Write the criterion task at the top of the design document and settle every subsequent argument against it: 'standing in front of a physical sign, in an unfamiliar display typeface, retrieve the meaning.' That is meaning-recall from a rendered form, not four-option discrimination. Never settle a design argument by asking 'is this deeper?'
directives.basis: Transfer-appropriate processing (Morris, Bransford & Franks 1977), verified by adversarial check; the levels-of-processing framework survives only in this form.

directives.directive: Reveal screen carries exactly one integration path: the target on its substrate, the meaning, and the one discriminating feature that is TRUE OF THIS ITEM AND FALSE OF THE LURE THE PLAYER ACTUALLY CHOSE. Everything else — component tree, confusable panel, mnemonic line, speed indicator — sits behind the explicit tap. The card must also thin out as an item's accuracy record improves.
directives.basis: Element interactivity, split attention and redundancy (Sweller; Mayer) plus expertise reversal (Chen, Kalyuga & Sweller 2017). Do NOT justify this with Cowan's ~4 — that derivation is graded folklore.

directives.directive: Pinyin renders as per-character syllables directly BELOW each character, baseline-aligned to that character's box (chū under 出, kǒu under 口). Never 'chūkǒu' as a single romanised string beside or under the word. The English/Dutch gloss attaches to the whole word directly under the pinyin row, never off to the side.
directives.basis: Lee & Kalyuga (2011), vertical-format advantage attributed to eliminating split attention — verified exactly by adversarial check.

directives.directive: Render the sign as a flat, high-contrast, information-bearing rectangle — plate, label, fascia, menu column, hazard board — with correct real-world colour inversion. No photographic street scene, no atmospheric gradient, no steam, no crowd, no perspective warp. Apply one test per pixel: does it constrain the meaning of the target? (¥ and the number on a price label: yes. The station plate's arrow: yes. Ambience: no.)
directives.basis: Seductive-details meta-analyses (Rey 2012; Sundararajan & Adesope 2020), with effects strongest under limited study time — the condition a timed, socially watched card creates.

directives.directive: Vary typeface and substrate ACROSS repeat exposures of the same item — the rule is 'do not repeat the substrate this item was last seen on'. Do not enforce non-repetition across different items within a round, and do not require a fixed number of typefaces per word.
directives.basis: High-variability orthographic training (Pelzl 2025) is single-session, n=190, 24 characters, no delayed test, effects of one-to-two words — a cheap default, not a numeric floor. The within-round non-repetition rule is self-defeating (a pure list of distinctive items) and trains against a substrate-homogeneous real register.

directives.directive: Distractor confusability is a pure function of the item's exposure state, never a difficulty dial: exposures 1–2 use semantically and visually UNRELATED distractors; component-sharing and confusable-family distractors unlock only after the item has been retrieved correctly across at least one intervening night. Log the distractor set alongside the outcome so this can be settled on your own data.
directives.basis: Little et al. (2012) exonerate competitive lures only where the learner can reject them from existing knowledge; Roediger & Marsh (2005) show the negative suggestion effect scales with lure plausibility; Butler & Roediger (2008) show feedback reduces but does not eliminate it.

directives.directive: Feedback is mandatory, immediate, in the same visual frame as the committed answer, and corrective rather than verdictive: show the correct answer, and when a lure was chosen, name that lure and mark it wrong explicitly. No round may end without correction. Record the specific chosen lure so the item's next exposure can re-present the discrimination that failed.
directives.basis: Butler & Roediger (2008); prequestion and pretesting effects require corrective feedback to exist at all; Nakata & Suzuki (2019) show harm surfaces as error type, not score.

directives.directive: Delete the forced re-tap of the visible correct answer. Replace with feedback → requeue at a delay.
directives.basis: Re-tapping a highlighted answer is copying, not retrieval; the prompts-beat-recasts result it rested on is about oral, ill-formed learner production in interaction.

directives.directive: Narrow the dealt category to prequestion granularity — 'signs on a subway platform', 'weight and price on a market label' — not 'Transport'. Guarantee that every bet resolves in the same round, and keep the scoring such that guessing stays attractive rather than driving players to hedge.
directives.basis: Prequestion meta-analysis: g = 0.66 for targeted information, no evidence of spread to non-targeted material in the same activity; unsuccessful pre-answer guesses are productive when feedback follows.

directives.directive: Add one meaning-recall beat: after answers lock but BEFORE the options/reveal, show the sign alone for ~3 s with 'say it out loud', then feedback. If it lands after the options are visible it is not a retrieval attempt and buys nothing. Log it as `spoken_attempt` for analysis only; do not score it.
directives.basis: Rowland (2014) format moderator — recognition practice tested by recognition is the weakest cell on both axes (g≈0.36 vs 0.70–0.79); the mitigation's own magnitude is unknown, so instrument it.

directives.directive: Say-it-aloud at reveal happens with the CHARACTER on screen, not pinyin alone, and every player produces (hearing others delivers far less than speaking). Rank it below the component breakdown and the confusable panel in the build order, and instrument it rather than assuming it.
directives.basis: Production effect is real, extends to recognition, and is larger in L2 — but here the produced token is pinyin rather than the target form, the pure-list between-subject variant is the smallest version, its mechanism is disputed, and unison group speech is untested.

directives.directive: One spoken self-explanation prompt at the reveal, on the confusable pair, addressed to the highest bettor: 'why isn't it 入口?' ~5 seconds, spoken to the table, never typed, never scored.
directives.basis: Bisra et al. (2018): g = 0.55 across 69 effect sizes / 64 reports / 20 moderators — verified exactly. Cheapest well-evidenced intervention in the cluster and it costs one line of text.

directives.directive: Any item missed at the HIGHEST bet tier is re-tested before the session ends, via a `high_confidence_miss` queue drained in the final round. Document that this is a massed repetition defended on hypercorrection grounds, not as scheduling.
directives.basis: Butler, Fazio & Marsh (2011): hypercorrection persists over a week, and a test after corrective feedback blocks the return of high-confidence errors. (Note the sweep misattributed this paper to Metcalfe & Finn.)

directives.directive: Log per attempt: item_id, chosen_option (not just correct/incorrect), bet_tier, was_correct, latency_ms, substrate/typeface id, scaffolding rung, role (answerer | observer), wall-clock timestamp, and time since last exposure. Maintain a per-user confusion matrix keyed on (target_item, chosen_item); when confusion[入口][出口] crosses a threshold, stop presenting them as co-options and re-teach the distinguishing component in isolation.
directives.basis: Nakata & Suzuki (2019): related and unrelated items did not differ in score at one week, but related items produced significantly more interference errors — a plain accuracy curve will look healthy while a pair is being cross-associated.

directives.directive: Two-bit item state per item per user: `acquired` (correct within the introducing session) and `consolidated` (correct on a retrieval that happened after at least one intervening night). Gate on the second bit: an item may not be used as a distractor for a confusable sibling, may not enter a component-contrast round, and may not count toward a mastery total until consolidated.
directives.basis: Dumay & Gaskell (2007) plus the storage-vs-retrieval-strength framing (Bjork & Bjork 1992). Present it as a cheap, low-risk design bet, not as established neuroscience — complementary-systems is a framework and the sleep-dependent competition result has null results and boundary conditions.

directives.directive: Scheduler: minimum inter-exposure gap is 'next session after the next sleep', never N hours. Store review events with wall-clock timestamps AND a boolean 'crossed a sleep period'. Never compute due-ness from session-relative counters.
directives.basis: Lexical integration tracks sleep rather than elapsed time (Dumay & Gaskell 2007); the modality-generalisation step to orthographic items is an explicit extrapolation — flag it as such in your own docs.

directives.directive: Do NOT ship `gap = 0.15 × (target_date − now)`. Condition the gap on estimated item strength as well as horizon: short gaps (one overnight) for an item's first two-to-three encounters regardless of trip date, widening only after successful cross-day retrievals. Let the trip date raise the RECALL THRESHOLD as it approaches, not shorten the gap directly. Equal intervals are a defensible v1; spend nothing on expanding-vs-equal tuning. Sibling-confusion events lower an item's strength estimate even when the answer was correct.
directives.basis: Cepeda's ratio is a two-session result on L1-comprehensible trivia on a flat, asymmetric optimum; Nakata (2015) finds expanding ≈ equal in L2; strength-based scheduling (Pavlik & Anderson; Half-Life Regression) is the validated replacement.

directives.directive: Make the primary mastery variable the number of distinct DAYS on which an item was successfully retrieved, and surface savings ('this sign took you three looks last month; one today') rather than a streak. Do not retire an item after N successes; if a retirement threshold ships, label it an unvalidated product decision.
directives.basis: Bahrick (1984): the durable plateau's height scales with the amount of ORIGINAL training, which argues for overlearning, not early retirement. Cross-sectional design with self-reported rehearsal — grade moderate.

directives.directive: Never enter both members of a form-confusable pair as new items in the same session. Add `confusion_type` with four values — form-confusable, meaning-confusable-visually-distinct, both, shared-morpheme — and a `family_id`. 麻/辣 may be shown together from day one; 公斤/斤 and 人/入 need staged introduction; 出口/入口 is the untested shared-morpheme case and should be instrumented separately.
directives.basis: Form similarity always increases confusion errors (Kemp 2021); semantic relatedness without form similarity helps in the L2→L1 direction this app tests; no cited study covers two-character shared-morpheme pairs, which is what the design's own flagship examples mostly are.

directives.directive: Pair-balanced testing: when any member of a confusable family is in the active deck, mark all members of that family due-soon so every member is tested within the same rotation window.
directives.basis: Retrieval-induced forgetting ≈ 8.7 percentage points, competition-dependent (Murayama et al. 2014). A deck that quizzes 出口 and never 入口 actively degrades 入口.

directives.directive: Every item with a form-confusable sibling ships one authored, meaning-bearing formula for the distinguishing component — required content, not flavour text. '出 = feet stepping out of an enclosure; 入 = a wedge entering.' At resolution the difference is named in words, not merely rendered adjacent.
directives.basis: Chang et al. (2022): the Pithy-Formulas-with-Key-images advantage over Key-images alone was SPECIFIC to the visually-similar-pair group; and the speech-perception training literature shows learners do not encode a confusable contrast unless attention is directed to the critical difference during learning.

directives.directive: Keep the task as identification ('what does this sign say?' / 'which of these is 出口?'). Never add a same/different mode, and never add a production mode (write, type, or produce the pinyin from the meaning). Store each item with exactly one tested direction, rendered_form → meaning, and no production field.
directives.basis: Identification-with-feedback beats same/different discrimination training; semantic relatedness helps in the L2→L1 comprehension direction and turns harmful in the L1→L2 production direction (Kemp 2021); mnemonic benefits, where they exist, are receptive only.

directives.directive: Mnemonic text: capped at one line, authored (never player-generated), derived from real components, marked `etymological` or `mnemonic-only`, and carrying ZERO scheduling weight — interval comes from the player's outcome, never from whether a mnemonic was shown. No Heisig/Blueprint/Chineasy-style invented scene per character. No bizarreness ratio. No memory-palace mode, no chain/journey through signs, no adjacency constraint on item selection.
directives.basis: All strategies were equal for READING in the best-controlled Chinese test (Chang et al. 2022); imagery mnemonics gave no advantage over rote beyond the immediate test on Chinese characters; method of loci is evidenced for immediate serial recall of word lists only; bizarreness is absent in cued recall and unreliable in recognition.

directives.directive: Write an exposure record for EVERY player at the table when an item resolves, flagged role: observer | answerer, and let observer exposures advance scheduling state at a discounted weight. Never show 'what everyone else picked' as a distribution bar; never surface a per-player accuracy leaderboard. Score the table against the item bank; bets are the only individual number on screen.
directives.basis: Observers gain from others' retrieval and collaborative retrieval improves later individual memory; social contagion means seeing another player's wrong answer implants it — a correctness requirement, not a comfort feature. Without observer records a player who watched thirty items and answered six is modelled as having seen six.

directives.directive: Track exposures per COMPONENT and per component×position, not only per word, and use them to bias item selection. Order content so high-frequency components appear early across many different characters and each component is seen in its legal position repeatedly before any item requires positional discrimination. Do not teach positional rules explicitly.
directives.basis: Orthographic regularity in Chinese is acquired by statistical learning in a fixed order (components → structure → positional legality), and positional knowledge is implicit and hard to acquire; component-level visual expertise is what transfers to unseen characters.

directives.directive: Experimentation policy, stated once at the top of the design doc: no learning-relevant feature may be killed or shipped on self-reported difficulty, perceived helpfulness, in-session accuracy, or session satisfaction. The only admissible primary metric is delayed accuracy at ≥1 week on TRANSFER items — real signage the player has never seen in training, in display and handwritten faces, at oblique angles, with the target embedded in a longer string. Report training-context accuracy and transfer accuracy side by side and expect a gap.
directives.basis: Learners' judgments are inverted for spacing, interleaving, retrieval practice and difficulty (Bjork, Dunlosky & Kornell 2013); the confusable panel will feel unpleasant and will be rated as making things harder. Recognition accuracy on the same stimulus in the same UI is the measure most inflated by item-specific and context learning.

directives.directive: Put an explicit exclusion list in the design document naming banned rationales: learning styles, the Ebbinghaus forgetting curve, 10,000 hours, the bizarreness effect, the method of loci, sleep audio / targeted memory reactivation, disfluent or degraded typefaces, and any forgetting-curve graphic or '70% by tomorrow' copy in the UI. Add the two sophisticated variants that DID appear: fMRI as a design warrant, and a working-memory capacity constant as a layout constant.
directives.basis: These absences were a decision, not an oversight, and a later revision will otherwise reintroduce them. The scheduler is where the forgetting curve always enters; any forgetting function must be fitted to the app's own per-item outcome data.

directives.directive: Audio is optional, never gating, never scored: store a per-user `audio_enabled` flag defaulting off, and ensure a player who never plays audio can reach every item and every score tier. Store `pinyin` (with tone marks) and `audio` on every item from day one even if v1 never surfaces them.
directives.basis: PSTM explains ~9–10% of variance in AUDITORY L2 vocabulary acquisition (r=.31), of unknown magnitude for orthographic learning in a logographic script — cheap insurance, not protection of 30% of anything. And excluding pronunciation is a scope decision that builds deliberately partial lexical representations; say so in the doc rather than dressing it as a finding.

directives.directive: End every session with one screen: 'you can now read these N signs', rendered as the actual signs at real size in their real typefaces. Never print a coverage percentage derived from a general-text character frequency list.
directives.basis: Demotivation converges on inability to perceive progress, and retrieval practice specifically confronts learners with their own non-mastery. General-corpus coverage figures do not transfer to signage (their top ranks are function morphemes) and token coverage is not sign comprehension on a four-character sign.

directives.directive: Read four papers in full before the build spec is frozen, because each one is load-bearing and none was read: Cao et al. (2013, J. Neurolinguistics 26(4), 440–461 — the only three-month Chinese-specific follow-up, and the true source of the chunking arithmetic); Brunmair & Richter (2019 — the composition and intervals of the 'words' moderator cell); Higa (1963 — the direction of the antonym effect, which decides whether 入口/出口 is the worst case or the easy one); and Li, Shi & Wang (2025 — the retention interval behind the paired-presentation and colour results). Mark each claim with a `verified_at` level (search-abstract vs full-text) rather than a blanket 'abstract-only'.
directives.basis: Search-level verification alone caught errors in six of fourteen checked claims across this cluster, and every error ran in the direction of making the recommendation sound more mandatory. 'I could not check it' is not a defence for a number that reaches a spec.

settled.claim: A published, downloadable, character-level frequency corpus of Chinese text in the urban wild EXISTS. CTW (Chinese Text in the Wild), Tsinghua/Tencent: 32,285 street-view images, 1,018,402 individually character-labelled instances, 3,850 distinct characters, annotations CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, baseline code MIT, and the shipped baseline already contains a STAT_FREQUENCY build step. RCTW-17 (12,263 images) corroborates.
settled.scope: Verified first-party from the project homepage source and repo. CTW is street-view imagery: it over-represents shopfront fascias and street signage, under-represents menus, shelf-edge labels and indoor plates. Its 'wordart' attribute confirms decorative display lettering is prevalent enough in real signage to need its own annotated class.
sources: Yuan, Zhu, Xu, Li, Mu & Hu (2019). A Large Chinese Text Dataset in the Wild. Journal of Computer Science and Technology 34(3):509-521 — https://ctwdataset.github.io/
https://github.com/yuantailing/ctw-baseline (judge/settings.py STAT_FREQUENCY; tutorial/1-basics.ipynb annotation format)
RCTW-17, ICDAR2017 Reading Chinese Text in the Wild, 12,263 images
settled.implication: Seed the item bank corpus-derived, not practitioner-derived. This kills the load-bearing negative finding that justified the peer-to-peer photo-capture architecture, and removes a PIPL/GDPR exposure. Capture drops from load-bearing to nice-to-have. Also use CTW to build the held-out sign set for the progress metric and the evaluation.

settled.claim: General-corpus character frequency is the wrong ordering key for signage, by roughly 10x at the top and it does not converge until ~2,500-3,000 characters. Of the top 50 characters by SUBTLEX-CH frequency exactly 4 are in the survival set (到 上 生 时), and arguably only 上 changes what you do at a sign; of the top 100, 15. At 1,000 frequency-ordered characters you hold 66% of the survival set, at 2,000 you hold 86%, and you need ~3,000 for 97%. 斤 is at frequency rank 2,551, 荤 4,012, 辣 1,420, 禁 1,140.
settled.scope: Computed this session over the real SUBTLEX-CH character table against a 200-character transcription of the survival set (median rank 702). Corrects the sweep's own estimate of a '2.5-3x gap converging at 1,200-1,500'.
sources: SUBTLEX-CH character frequency table (Cai & Brysbaert 2010, PLoS ONE 5(6):e10729), full data file read this session — https://github.com/glxxyz/hskhsk.com
Computation recorded at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-dohhh/4806d96a-ebd4-5774-9d7d-fe7e365865df/scratchpad/survival.py
settled.implication: Never seed or sort the bank from a frequency list. Store freqRank as a tie-breaker field only. This is the single strongest argument in the whole cluster for a bespoke functional ordering, and it is stronger than the sweep claimed.

settled.claim: HSK gives you two thirds of the bricks and almost none of the buildings — measured, not estimated. Of a 480-item survival set (214 characters, 266 compounds): 87.9% is absent from HSK 2.0 levels 1-3; only 63.6% of survival CHARACTERS appear in HSK 3.0's first 900; only 15.4% of survival COMPOUNDS appear in HSK 3.0 levels 1-3 (39% appear anywhere in all 11,092 words; 162 of 266 appear at no level at all, including 换乘 安全出口 净含量 冷藏 时价 单程票 二等座 无障碍 扶梯 干煸 会员价 买一送一 去结算 提交订单 售罄 托运 改签 失物招领). The character/compound gap is 48 points.
settled.scope: Computed against the official GF 0025-2021 character and word lists and the official HSK 2.0 (2012) word lists, both parsed this session. The sweep predicted 75-82% / 75-85% / 35-45% and was too generous to HSK every time.
sources: 国际中文教育中文水平等级标准 GF 0025-2021 official lists via https://github.com/elkmovie/hsk30 (cumulative counts independently confirmed: L1 500/300, L1-2 1272/600, L1-3 2245/900, L1-4 3245/1200, L1-6 5456/1800, L1-9 11092/3000)
HSK 2.0 official word lists (2012) via https://github.com/glxxyz/hskhsk.com (per-level sizes confirmed 150/150/300/600/1300/2500)
settled.implication: The missing third of the bricks is not random: it is exactly the cooking methods (炒炸煮蒸烤焖炖涮拌卤烧煎爆), the organ terms (肠肚肝肺肾腰舌筋) and 禁 折 质 藏 冻 辣 咸 酸 鲜 素 荤. Do not market or seed as 'HSK 1 for travellers'. Do import the numeral/date/time subset wholesale — the one place HSK and signage genuinely coincide.

settled.claim: 93% of the survival set is inside the official 3,000-character standard, but smeared across all nine levels. Of 214 survival characters: 67 at L1, 38 at L2, 31 at L3, 21 at L4, 13 at L5, 15 at L6, 15 at L7-9, and 14 outside the 3,000 entirely (壹贰叁肆伍陆柒捌玖拾佰仟 plus 焖 胗 荤 蟹 蹄 驴).
settled.scope: Computed against the GF 0025-2021 official 3,000-character reading list.
sources: GF 0025-2021 official character list via https://github.com/elkmovie/hsk30 (charlist.txt)
settled.implication: The pitch is not 'we teach rare characters'. It is 'none of this is obscure — 93% is in the official 3,000-character standard, just spread across nine levels of a ladder built for a different purpose, so no course reaches it for years.' The 14 out-of-standard characters are almost all the financial capital numerals, confirming their low-priority 'bank counter' sub-deck. Move 焖 胗 蟹 蹄 驴 to Tier 2; keep 荤 in Tier 0 because it pairs with 素 and protects a dietary flag.

settled.claim: The Chinese state's own standard already decouples reading from handwriting, at 3:1. GF 0025-2021 specifies 3,000 characters for RECOGNITION across nine levels, plus three separate and much smaller 手写字表 handwriting lists: 初等 300, 中等 400, 高等 500 — 1,200 total. At the elementary stage a learner is expected to recognise 900 characters and to write only 300.
settled.scope: Structure read and counted directly from the official list this session.
sources: 国际中文教育中文水平等级标准 GF 0025-2021, official character list — https://github.com/elkmovie/hsk30
settled.implication: This is the best available answer to the 'but handwriting is essential for hanzi' objection, and it comes from the authority the objection appeals to. Put it in the about screen and the funding deck with the numbers. Honest counterweight: Guan et al. (2011) is real evidence that writing builds the orthographic representation recognition depends on, so a reading-only product is making a considered trade, not a free choice.

settled.claim: The flesh radical in 肠 肚 肝 肺 肾 腰 脑 胗 is ⺼ (U+2EBC, Kangxi 130 肉), NOT 月 (U+6708, moon, Kangxi 74). They are homoglyphs in almost every font and different codepoints.
settled.scope: Verified independently this session against makemeahanzi (9,574 entries): all eight organ characters carry radical ⺼ U+2EBC; 期 and 朋 carry 月 U+6708. Correct exception list for the organ set: 血 (radical 血), 皮 (radical 皮) and 舌 (radical 舌, ⿱千口) do NOT carry it; 筋 carries it inside 肋 (⿱⺮肋, 肋 = ⿰⺼力) but takes ⺮ as its Kangxi radical.
sources: makemeahanzi character database, radical + decomposition fields — https://github.com/skishore/makemeahanzi
Unicode: U+2EBC KANGXI RADICAL MEAT vs U+6708 CJK UNIFIED IDEOGRAPH-6708
settled.implication: Any implementation that string-matches or regex-matches on 月 to apply the component accent colour highlights ZERO of the six target characters and fires instead on 期 — which sits inside 保质期, a Tier-1 item. It fails silently and teaches the wrong thing. Key highlighting off a stored per-item component field or a decomposition database, never off a substring match.

settled.claim: The simplified food radical is 饣 (43 common characters: 饭 饿 馆 饺 饼 饮 馒 饥 饰 饱 饲 …), not 食 (12, mostly traditional or rare: 食 飧 飨 餍 餐 餮 饔 饕). And the highest-value radical for menu reading is 火/灬: 9 of the 13 core cooking-method characters take it as their radical (炒 爆 炸 煮 烤 焖 炖 烧 煎), and 蒸 contains 灬 inside 烝.
settled.scope: Verified independently this session against makemeahanzi radical counts: 饣=43, 食=12, 火=128, 灬=28, 刂=71, 阝=160, 讠=144, 钅=223, 纟=143, 亻=277, 氵=467.
sources: makemeahanzi radical field — https://github.com/skishore/makemeahanzi
settled.implication: A learner taught 食 as 'the food radical' will not recognise it in 饭馆 or 饺子 — precisely the words the product targets. Validate the whole onboarding radical list against simplified component forms, not dictionary/traditional head forms: the same trap applies to 讠/言, 钅/金, 纟/糸, 饣/食, 见/見. 餐 does contain 食 but as a bottom component, so it does not rescue the choice.

settled.claim: Character structure statistics are inversely related to frequency, so whole-script figures do not describe this product's bank. Pictophonetic share by frequency band: ranks 1-100 = 28.8%, 101-300 = 37.7%, 301-600 = 53.0%, 601-1000 = 66.3%, 2001-3500 = 79.6%, whole dictionary = 77.1%. In the top 1,000: 53.1% pictophonetic, 37.8% ideographic, 9.1% pictographic. In the literal first 50 characters only 12/50 are pictophonetic — 一 是 人 了 不 大 中 国 are not decomposable into meaning+sound.
settled.scope: Computed over makemeahanzi etymology (n=9,574) crossed with a jieba-derived character frequency ranking. Absolute percentages are soft (makemeahanzi etymology is compiled from secondary sources and its 'ideographic' bucket probably absorbs opaque compounds), but labelling bias largely cancels in the within-dataset band comparison.
sources: Computed: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skishore/makemeahanzi/master/dictionary.txt
Computed: frequency from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fxsjy/jieba/master/jieba/dict.txt
Shu, Chen, Anderson, Wu & Xuan (2003), Child Development 74(1) — the ~80% whole-script figure; abstract-only, not re-verified
settled.implication: Pictographs and ideographs are ~47% of the core bank, not a <10% edge case. A non-phonetic-compound explanation path — pictographic/ideographic origin, or an explicit 'no useful decomposition, learn as a whole' state — is required for roughly half the early bank.

settled.claim: Left-right structure and the meaning-slot/sound-slot card cover far less of the early bank than the literature figure suggests. Top-level ⿰ is 58.1% of all 3,500 Tier-1 characters, 44.8% of the top 1,000, 40.0% of the top 600, 30.0% of the top 100. The intersection that a two-slot meaning/sound card honestly describes (left-right AND phonetic) is 13.0% of the top 100, 24.2% of the top 600, 30.7% of the top 1,000, 46.1% of Tier-1. Semantic-component-on-the-left within left-right phonetic compounds is confirmed at 89.9% dictionary-wide (n=5,024) but only 76.8% in ranks 1-300 and 83.9% in the top 1,000.
settled.scope: Computed over makemeahanzi decomposition/radical fields and the 2013 通用规范汉字表 Tier 1 (verified at exactly 3,500 characters). Hsiao & Shillcock's ~72% is 72% OF PHONOGRAMS, not of all characters — the sweep swapped the denominator.
sources: Computed: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skishore/makemeahanzi/master/dictionary.txt
Computed: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shengdoushi/common-standard-chinese-characters-table/master/level-1.txt
Hsiao & Shillcock (2006), J. Psycholinguistic Research 35:405-426 — abstract-only, not re-verified
settled.implication: A two-slot meaning/sound card must be a conditional layout selected off a stored structure+etymology enum, never the default. Budget at least three more layouts (top-bottom, enclosure, atomic/unanalysable) covering the majority of early items. Teach 'left side = what it is about' as a strong tendency, not a rule, when teaching it early.

settled.claim: The phonetic component is far less reliable in the core bank than dictionary-wide. Top 1,000 (n=438 scored): exact match including tone 16.9%, segmental match only 21.7%, rime-only 26.0%, NO CUE AT ALL 35.4%. Top 2,500 (n=1,383): exact 23.0%. Whole dictionary (n=6,788): exact 34.3%, no cue 29.0%. Reliability roughly doubles between the top 1,000 and the full dictionary.
settled.scope: Computed by comparing each character's primary Unihan reading to its phonetic component's primary reading. Primary-reading-only comparison; polyphony and phonetic-component identification add noise. Bank-specific estimates, not literature constants.
sources: Computed: makemeahanzi etymology.phonetic field — https://github.com/skishore/makemeahanzi
Computed: Unihan-derived readings — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozillazg/pinyin-data/master/pinyin.txt
settled.implication: In the core bank the phonetic hint is fully right about 1 time in 6 and gives no usable cue about 1 time in 3. Gate the feature on a computed per-character reliability field, suppress it entirely for the ~35% no-cue set, and never let copy imply a rule. The feature is worth more at intermediate level than at beginner level — the opposite of where it would naturally be surfaced.

settled.claim: Pronunciation is a property of a token in context, not of a character. 1,378 of 3,500 Tier-1 characters (39.4%) carry more than one Unihan reading; 28.5% have more than one distinct segmental syllable and 10.9% differ by tone alone. The heteronyms saturate this exact domain: 行 háng in 银行 but xíng in 人行道 and 行李 (行李寄存 at every station); 便 biàn in 方便 but pián in 便宜; 地 dì in 小心地滑 but de as an adverbial marker; 了 le in 卖完了 but liǎo in 了解; also 长 cháng/zhǎng, 重 zhòng/chóng, 少 shǎo/shào, 还 hái/huán, 干 gān/gàn, 得 dé/de/děi, 好 hǎo/hào, 中 zhōng/zhòng, 发 fā/fà, 乐 lè/yuè, 调 diào/tiáo.
settled.scope: Computed over Unihan crossed with 通用规范汉字表 Tier 1. The 39.4% is an upper bound (Unihan includes obsolete literary readings) but the practical head of the list is unavoidable.
sources: Computed: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozillazg/pinyin-data/master/pinyin.txt × https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shengdoushi/common-standard-chinese-characters-table/master/level-1.txt
settled.implication: A per-character form→sound field is ill-defined for a large minority of core items: a card showing 行 alone and asking 'which pinyin?' has two correct answers, and a naive per-character pinyin generator gets 小心地滑 — the most famous sign in China — wrong. Key pinyin to (token, word-context), carry a heteronym flag, and never ask for a character's pronunciation in isolation.

settled.claim: Displayed citation pinyin systematically contradicts natural audio, and it does so exactly at the T2/T3 boundary learners are weakest on. Third-tone sandhi (T3+T3 → T2+T3) applies in 水饺 shuǐjiǎo→shuíjiǎo, 米粉 mǐfěn→mífěn, 老板 lǎobǎn→láobǎn, 两碗 liǎng wǎn→liáng wǎn, 九点 jiǔdiǎn→jiúdiǎn. 不 bù → bú before a fourth tone (不是 búshì, 不要 búyào, 不对 búduì). 一 yī → yì before T1/T2/T3 and → yí before T4 (一点 yìdiǎn, 一起 yìqǐ, 一个 yíge). 一 and 不 are frequency rank 1 and 5. Neutral tone is a further channel: 东西 dōngxi 'thing' vs dōngxī 'east-west'.
settled.scope: Descriptive Mandarin phonology, checkable in any reference grammar; frequency ranks computed this session. Note 好吃 hǎochī is T3+T1 — only allophonic half-third lowering applies, so it does NOT motivate a stored surface-tone field.
sources: Chen, M. Y. (2000). Tone Sandhi: Patterns across Chinese Dialects. Cambridge University Press
Standard descriptive Mandarin phonology (Chao, Duanmu) — not a contested area
Computed frequency ranks from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fxsjy/jieba/master/jieba/dict.txt
settled.implication: Store pinyin_citation and pinyin_surface as separate per-token fields with an explicit neutral-tone state, render surface form whenever audio is present, and flag sandhi items out of any tone-scoring drill. Otherwise the app displays a T3 while playing a T2 on exactly the items where the learner is weakest — actively training the confusion it is trying to prevent.

settled.claim: T2/T3 is the dominant tone error for non-tonal-L1 adults including Dutch speakers specifically, and it is acoustically driven rather than L1-driven — English, Dutch and even Cantonese L1 learners all show it. The discriminating cue is the timing of the F0 turning point (near onset for T2, mid for T3); L2 listeners lean on duration instead. Dutch beginners process segmental and tonal information separately, like Dutch listeners with no Mandarin at all, and integrate them only at advanced level; advanced Dutch learners improved on T2/T3 sub-lexically but NOT in lexical decision.
settled.scope: Abstract-only throughout; downgraded from the sweep's 'strong' because no full text was opened and no publication-bias diagnostic was reported. Zou, Caspers & Chen is the only body of work on Dutch L1 Mandarin learners. Expanding F0 range reduces the T2-as-T3 error only slightly (0.30 → 0.27), which is evidence the confusion is categorical, not audibility-limited.
sources: Zou, T., Caspers, J. & Chen, Y. (2022). Perception of Different Tone Contrasts at Sub-Lexical and Lexical Levels by Dutch Learners of Mandarin Chinese. Frontiers in Psychology 13:891756 — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35734459/
Zou, T. (2017). Production and perception of tones by Dutch learners of Mandarin. PhD diss., Leiden / LOT 472 — https://scholarlypublications.universiteitleiden.nl/handle/1887/52977
Hao, Y.-C. (2012). Journal of Phonetics 40(2) — https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S009544701100101X
settled.implication: Never let a T2/T3 discrimination gate progress. Exclude the T2↔T3 swap from the pinyin distractor pool for the first 200 items and score T2/T3 as a single merged category until a player has cleared a dedicated opt-in contrast drill. Do not draw the four tones as symmetric icons — if tone is visualised at all, mark the turning point, because that is the cue learners are missing.

settled.claim: Colour and extra visual salience applied to the glyph hurt L2 character recognition. Radical colour markings increased reaction times and decreased accuracy; stroke-order animations also decreased recognition accuracy; neither affected character-meaning matching. Independently, colour coding slowed reaction times in a 2×2×2 study of absolute beginners, interpreted as visual overload.
settled.scope: Hou & Jiang (2022) is N=40 alphabetic-L1 learners, within-subjects, abstract-only. Li, Shi & Wang (2025) is N=183 non-tonal-L1 absolute beginners, abstract-only. Both are recognition-time manipulations — they say nothing against teaching components as content in a separate lesson or reveal.
sources: Hou, F. & Jiang, X. (2022). Interference effects of radical markings and stroke order animations on Chinese character learning among L2 learners. Frontiers in Psychology 13:783613

Li, J., Shi, M. & Wang, X. (2025). Learning Chinese Characters of Visual Similarity: The Effects of Presentation Style and Color Coding. Languages 10(10):260 — https://doi.org/10.3390/languages10100260
Chen, H.-C. et al. (2013). Language Learning & Technology 17(1), N=129, 3 weeks — the FOR side: explicit radical instruction raises phonetic- and semantic-radical awareness
settled.implication: Split the two surfaces. Component colour, animation and decomposition live in the lesson and the reveal; the timed recognition card renders the hanzi as a single solid-colour glyph on a plain ground, no highlighting, no stroke animation. Reserve colour for scoring and turn state.

settled.claim: Simultaneous paired presentation of visually similar characters improves discrimination of subtle stroke differences in absolute beginners, and characters differing by an added stroke (日/白) are easier than identical-stroke pairs (人/入). Visual similarity, not phonology, drives the large majority of character errors.
settled.scope: Li, Shi & Wang (2025), N=183 non-tonal-L1 absolute beginners, abstract-only. The error-rate statistics the sweep quoted (75% of 4,100 miswritten characters; 4,305 responses from 144 CSL learners) are effectively UNSOURCED — they were attributed solely to a mnemonics intervention study that cannot be their origin. The paired-presentation result stands; the error percentages do not.
sources: Li, J., Shi, M. & Wang, X. (2025). Languages 10(10):260 — https://doi.org/10.3390/languages10100260
Chang, L.-Y., Tang, Y.-Y., Lee, C.-Y. & Chen, H.-C. (2022). Frontiers in Psychology 13:783898 — abstract-only; NOT a source for the 75%/4,100 error figures
settled.implication: Introduce confusables as a side-by-side pair, not one at a time: 人/入, 日/白, 千/干, 未/末, 出/山, 天/夭, 士/土, 己/已, 大/太, 微/徽. Generate distractors visual-first from a stored orthographic-neighbour list, not from same-pinyin or same-meaning sets — but only with mandatory immediate feedback (see the lure-implantation finding).

settled.claim: Multiple choice implants false knowledge from the lures, and the risk is highest exactly where the distractors are most plausible — i.e. under a visual-first distractor rule. Immediate corrective feedback substantially reduces or eliminates the effect.
settled.scope: Roediger & Marsh (2005) and Butler & Roediger (2008) cited from knowledge, not retrieved. Well-replicated, textbook-level. Concrete failure mode here: a player who saw 冷冻 as a lure on the 冷藏 item and is now unsure which one means refrigerate.
sources: Roediger, H. L. & Marsh, E. J. (2005). The positive and negative consequences of multiple-choice testing. JEP:LMC 31(5):1155-1159
Butler, A. C. & Roediger, H. L. (2008). Feedback enhances the positive effects and reduces the negative effects of multiple-choice testing. Memory & Cognition 36(3):604-616
settled.implication: Never end a round without showing the correct answer paired with the item. The reveal must gloss all four options, not mark one — a four-row table, not a green tick.

settled.claim: Chinese public signage is a subjectless, function-word-free telegraphic register: imperative or nominal, with no 的, no aspect markers and no pronouns. 禁止吸烟, 小心地滑, 请勿触摸, 严禁烟火, 营业中, 暂停服务, 卖完了, 推, 拉, 出口, 请扫码点单.
settled.scope: Descriptive and internally verifiable against the item set itself. This refutes the proposed lint rule 'reject items whose segmentation lacks an overt subject when a verb is present' — that rule would reject 禁止吸烟, 小心地滑, 请勿触摸 and 卖完了 and empty the bank.
sources: Internal consistency check against the cluster's own tier-1 exemplars

Jin, H. G. (1994). Topic-Prominence and Subject-Prominence in L2 Acquisition. Language Learning, ERIC EJ483574 — the topic-prominence transfer finding, which concerns connected prose and does not transfer to fixed signage
settled.implication: Signage strings are learned as atomic whole units, so topic-prominence transfer is not a live risk in tiers 0-2. If a lint rule is wanted, make it the opposite: flag any item that is a full sentence with an overt subject as out-of-domain for a signage deck. Ship directional-complement signs (入口, 出口, 上车, 下车, 进站, 出站, 过街, 回收) as whole two-character units tagged atomic, never decomposed into a complement analysis.

settled.claim: Character coverage is not item readability, and the arithmetic is brutal. Knowing 40% of characters gives P(reading a whole 4-character dish name) ≈ 0.40^4 ≈ 2.6%, not 40%. At 75% coverage it is ≈ 32%. At 89% coverage a 6-character sign has ≈ 50% chance of containing at least one unknown character. Moving 1,000→3,000 characters takes coverage 89%→99%, removing ~90% of the remaining unknowns — so in a Zipfian tail the last decile of coverage is where whole-item readability is won.
settled.scope: Arithmetic over the coverage figures themselves; needs no source. Independence is a generous approximation. Corrects the sweep's claim that 'character 1,001 is worth two orders of magnitude less than character 10', which inverts the economics.
sources: Analytic — arithmetic, verifiable without a source
settled.implication: A 600-900 character target is probably UNDER-scoped, not over-scoped, for whole-sign readability. Never promise 'read 40% of a menu' from 40% character coverage. Set tier targets by simulating whole-item read rate over the domain corpus.

settled.claim: Coverage curves are register-dependent by several points and neither available corpus is signage. Two independent derivations this session: jieba-lexicon-weighted gives top 100 = 35.8%, top 500 = 72.7%, top 1,000 = 87.1%, top 2,500 = 97.6%, top 3,500 = 99.0%; SUBTLEX-CH gives top 1,000 = 93.97%, top 2,000 = 98.86%, top 3,000 = 99.81%. Both reproduce the official 现代汉语常用字表 tail anchors (2,500 = 97.97%, 3,500 = 99.48%) but disagree by ~5-7 points at rank 1,000. The two lists do not even agree on their top three: Jun Da opens 的 一 是 了, SUBTLEX-CH opens 我 的 你 (subtitles inflate second-person pronouns and speech verbs).
settled.scope: Both curves computed this session. The widely quoted 'top 100 ≈ 42%, top 1,000 ≈ 90%' figures are secondary-source compilations of one upstream list (Jun Da), not three independent corpora, and lingua.mtsu.edu was unreachable.
sources: Computed: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fxsjy/jieba/master/jieba/dict.txt
Computed: SUBTLEX-CH-CHR full table (46,841,097 characters / 33,546,516 words / 6,243 films — header confirmed) via https://github.com/glxxyz/hskhsk.com
settled.implication: Quote no coverage percentage in product copy. Two corpora both called 'Chinese character frequency' disagreeing on their top three is itself the compact demonstration of why neither should seed a signage curriculum — quote CTW instead.

settled.claim: Simplified→traditional is one-to-many and the ambiguity is concentrated in the highest-frequency and most food-domain characters. 277 of 4,013 simplified characters (6.9%) map to two or more traditional forms: 面→麵/麪 vs 面, 发→發/髮, 干→乾/幹/干/榦, 后→後/后, 里→裏/裡/里/哩, 台→臺/檯/颱/台, 只→只/隻/祇, 几→幾/几, 出→出/齣, 了→了/瞭, 复→復/複/覆, 系→系/係/繫, 松→鬆/松, 谷→谷/穀, 历→歷/曆, 钟→鍾/鐘.
settled.scope: Computed from OpenCC's STCharacters table (4,013 entries). Correct conversion is word-level and context-dependent, not character-level.
sources: Computed: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BYVoid/OpenCC/master/data/dictionary/STCharacters.txt
Computed: TSCharacters.txt
settled.implication: A single nullable traditional column silently picks one form and renders wrong text — 头发 → 頭發 instead of 頭髮, 牛肉面 → 牛肉面 instead of 牛肉麵, 理发 instead of 理髮, 肉松 instead of 肉鬆. Store a nullable LIST plus a word-level override table, or store nothing and defer. Add a lint rule flagging any item containing 面/干/发/后/里/松/只/几/表/系/术 for manual traditional review.

settled.claim: Traditional forms are legal and common on real mainland shopfront fascias, which is the one domain the product ranks third by payoff. Chinese language law permits 繁体字 in enumerated cases including calligraphic and handwritten shop signs (题词和招牌的手书字), and fascias favour exactly that lettering. CTW's annotation schema needs a dedicated 'wordart' attribute for decorative lettering, corroborating that display typography is prevalent in street-view Chinese text.
settled.scope: The article text of 《中华人民共和国国家通用语言文字法》 (2000) Art. 17 was not retrievable (gov.cn 403-blocked); verify before quoting. The one-to-many mappings were verified with OpenCC.
sources: 《中华人民共和国国家通用语言文字法》 (2000), Article 17 — not verified this session
OpenCC one-to-many mappings verified — https://github.com/BYVoid/OpenCC
Yuan et al. (2019) CTW 'wordart' attribute — https://ctwdataset.github.io/
settled.implication: Ship simplified only (the mainland legal mandate for public and official use is sound), but add an optional tradVariants[] per item populated by OpenCC at build time, and in the shopfront-fascia template only, present the traditional form for a small share of presentations. A learner who has only met simplified 面 will not recognise 麵館 on a calligraphic noodle-shop fascia — and 面馆 is Tier 1. This also makes the app usable in Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan with no second content set.

settled.claim: HSK 3.0 band order IS strongly frequency-aligned, band sizes are uneven, and HSK beats raw frequency on exactly this product's vocabulary. Median frequency rank rises monotonically across bands: 291, 479, 674, 872, 1302, 1702, 2637; the share of each band inside the top 1,000 falls monotonically 88%→79%→69%→57%→34%→13%→2%. Per-band new-character counts are 246 / 125 / 284 / 441 / 431 / 413 / 1,148, not '~300'. And 厕 is frequency rank 3,107 but sits in HSK 4; 禁 (947) and 止 (735) likewise appear at HSK 4.
settled.scope: Computed from the HSK 3.0 hanzi lists (community OCR of the official syllabus; totals ~3,088 vs the official 3,000, so ~3% noise, but the shape is unambiguous). Verify per-band counts against GF 0025-2021 before printing any band label.
sources: Computed: https://github.com/krmanik/HSK-3.0
Computed: frequency ranking from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fxsjy/jieba/master/jieba/dict.txt
settled.implication: Do not demote HSK to a display label. It is a frequency-correlated ordering that additionally corrects for concreteness and practical utility in ways news-corpus frequency does not — a pure frequency-band scheme would place 厕 at band 63 and never teach it. Use a blended ordering (functional payoff × HSK band × frequency as tie-breaker), not strict frequency bands of 50.

settled.claim: Mandarin offers no cognates to Dutch or English, so every item is a pure arbitrary paired associate — form, sound and meaning all novel. Cognate facilitation is one of the most replicated effects in bilingual lexical processing and survives into learning, not just processing.
settled.scope: Downgraded from the sweep's 'strong': abstract-only, no bias diagnostic. The retrieval-count implication (~8-12 successful retrievals rather than 3-4) is an inference from the absence of facilitation, not a measured figure for Chinese.
sources: Sanahuja, N. & Erdocia, K. (2024). The impact of cognate vocabulary on explicit L2 rule learning. Language Teaching Research — https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/13621688241254617
Chen et al. (2025). The Cognate Facilitation Effect of L2–L3 Cognates in Chinese–English–Spanish Trilinguals. IJAL — https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/ijal.70330
settled.implication: Budget far more exposures per item than a European-language app would, and size the bank accordingly. Do not import retention assumptions from Spanish or German vocabulary apps.

settled.claim: Glossing beats no glossing and L1 glosses beat L2 glosses, but the effect is small and the studies do not match this product's task. Two meta-analyses agree on direction: Kim, Lee & Lee (78 effect sizes, 26 studies, N=2,189) put L1 over L2 at Hedges' g = 0.33, clearest for beginners and on immediate posttests; Yanagisawa, Webb & Uchihara (359 effect sizes, 42 studies, N=3,802) find glossed > unglossed and L1 > L2, with multiple-choice glosses the most effective gloss type and in-text glosses and glossaries the least.
settled.scope: Downgraded from 'strong': abstract-only, no bias diagnostic, and g = 0.33 is a small effect. Critically, in that literature a gloss is met WHILE READING A TEXT, where sentence context constrains the choice. This product has no text — it is context-free isolated cards — so the gloss-type moderator does not transfer, and the moderator is confounded with an added retrieval demand anyway (a multiple-choice gloss is a gloss plus a test). Chen (2025, TESOL Quarterly) dissents, reporting both gloss languages at medium effect.
sources: Kim, H. S., Lee, J. H. & Lee, H. The relative effects of L1 and L2 glosses on L2 learning: A meta-analysis. Language Teaching Research — https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/full/10.1177/1362168820981394 (note: the sweep dated this 2024 but the DOI is a 2020-series identifier; fix or drop the year)
Yanagisawa, A., Webb, S. & Uchihara, T. How do different forms of glossing contribute to L2 vocabulary learning from reading? SSLA
Chen, X. (2025). The Effects of Gloss Language on L2 Vocabulary Learning from Reading. TESOL Quarterly — https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/tesq.3394
settled.implication: Keep the 4-option meaning choice, but justify it from retrieval practice, not from the gloss-type moderator. Default the gloss to the user's L1 (Dutch for nl locale, English otherwise) as a reasonable prior, store gloss: {nl, en} on every item from day one, render one and put the other behind a tap on the answer side — and instrument it, because the literature cannot settle the Dutch–English–Mandarin triad.

settled.claim: Pinyin layout is a split-attention problem with a measured answer, and learner preference does not track learning. Vertical format (pinyin directly under each character) significantly beat the conventional horizontal format (pinyin after the string). A later study (N=69 English natives, 30 Chinese words) compared horizontal / vertical / adjacent and found the adjacent format produced the highest gain scores — and was the LEAST preferred, with preference ratings unrelated to gains. Acquisition was also faster when the character was presented BEFORE rather than after the pinyin/English prompts.
settled.scope: Abstract-only. Lee & Kalyuga (2011) Language Learning 61(4):1099-1118; Chung (2007) Educational Psychology 27(1):1-20; SSLA (2023) N=69.
sources: Lee, C. H. & Kalyuga, S. (2011). Effectiveness of Different Pinyin Presentation Formats in Learning Chinese Characters. Language Learning 61(4) — https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ945914
Chung, K. K. H. (2007). Presentation factors in the learning of Chinese characters. Educational Psychology 27(1) — https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/01443410601061306
How to present L2 Chinese words effectively for learning (2023). SSLA
settled.implication: Where pinyin appears at all (reveal side only), render it directly beneath each individual character, per-character aligned, never as one string under the whole word; gloss adjacent, not on a distant line. Show the hanzi first, alone, for a beat. And ignore player preference surveys about layout.

settled.claim: Chinese has no word spaces and word segmentation is a genuine, measurable L2 bottleneck: L2 readers fall back to character-by-character reading. Word-spaced text produces the least disruption, unspaced more, character-spaced more still, and NONWORD-spaced text the most — so the benefit comes from correct word boundaries, not from white space per se.
settled.scope: Multiple independent eye-tracking labs, abstract-only. Tension the evidence does not resolve: all real signage and menus are unspaced, so spacing is a scaffold that must be removed before transfer.
sources: Eye movements of second language learners when reading spaced and unspaced Chinese texts (2023). Frontiers in Psychology 14:783960
Unpacking word segmentation processes by L2 Chinese readers: Evidence from eye movements. Bilingualism: Language and Cognition
The Impact of Color Cues on Word Segmentation by L2 Chinese Readers (2025). Behavioral Sciences 15(7):904 — https://doi.org/10.3390/bs15070904
settled.implication: Store every reading string pre-segmented into word tokens at authoring time — a stored field, never computed on device. Render a subtle per-word background tint (not spaces, which change layout, and not per-character colour) in beginner mode, collapsing to zero as the item is mastered, and make the final review of every item unspaced.

settled.claim: Chinese needs a larger rendered size than Latin at equivalent legibility, and the binding variable is stroke density — roughly 0.25 arcmin of extra character size per additional stroke, with stroke WIDTH becoming critical above ~15 strokes. But the survival set is far less dense than claimed once the correct simplified forms are used.
settled.scope: Direction reliable; magnitude approximate. The primary studies (Cai, Chi & You 2001; Liu & Yu 2016; Huang, Rau & Liu 2009) are 10-25-year-old display ergonomics on desktop/VR, predating high-DPI phones, and were not retrieved. Stroke counts verified this session: 警 19, 藏 17, 燥 17, 糖 16, 醋 15, 辣 14, 蒸 13, 酱 13 are genuinely dense in SIMPLIFIED; but 检 is 11 (not 17), 质 8, 边 5, 咸 9, 饺 9, 摊 13, 药 9 — the sweep's clinching examples 檢 續 醬 鹹 餃 質 藥 攤 邊 are TRADITIONAL forms and do not belong in a simplified-only product.
sources: Cai, D., Chi, C.-F. & You, M. (2001). The legibility threshold of Chinese characters in three type styles. IJIE 27(1):9-17
Liu, N. & Yu, R. (2016). Effects of Font Size, Stroke Width, and Character Complexity on the Legibility of Chinese Characters. HFEM
Stroke counts verified this session against makemeahanzi graphics.txt — https://github.com/skishore/makemeahanzi
settled.implication: Gate any render-size bump on a real stored strokeCount, never a hand-picked list. Use Medium/Regular or heavier — never Light or Thin — because stroke width is the constraint on complex glyphs. Treat all specific pixel figures as a starting point for an in-house legibility test on target devices, not as a spec: no study reports them.

settled.claim: The font strategy fails in the only country the app exists for, and the fix is measured. fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com are blocked in mainland China, so a Google-Fonts-served Noto Sans SC falls back to the system CJK face exactly where it matters — which is the Japanese-locale glyph-form failure the design is trying to avoid for 直 骨 每 令 画. Measured: NotoSansSC-Regular.otf = 7.95 MB (VF = 15.05 MB); a pyftsubset woff2 of 482 glyphs (378 CJK + Latin + digits + tone-marked vowels + punctuation) = 60.0 KB, a 135× reduction. Three faces (sans 400, sans 700, serif 400) ≈ 180 KB. Google Fonts also serves CJK as ~100 unicode-range-sliced woff2 files fetched lazily per codepoint range, which is close to unusable for a service-worker-precached offline PWA even where reachable.
settled.scope: Font sizes and the subset were measured this session with fontTools. Mainland blocking of Google hosts is documented but not verifiable from this sandbox — confirm from a mainland vantage before ship; the engineering fix is correct regardless.
sources: Measured this session: NotoSansSC-Regular.otf from https://github.com/notofonts/noto-cjk (Sans/SubsetOTF/SC) = 7.95 MB; subset via pyftsubset = 60.0 KB woff2 / 66.3 KB woff
Command: pyftsubset NotoSansSC-Regular.otf --text-file=bank-chars.txt --flavor=woff2 --layout-features= --no-hinting --desubroutinize
settled.implication: Self-host a subset generated at build time from the item bank's own character inventory, so the font can never drift from the content, and precache it in the service worker. Pinyin tone marks need the Latin Extended ranges (ā á ǎ à ē é ě è ī í ǐ ì ō ó ǒ ò ū ú ǔ ù ǖ ǘ ǚ ǜ) — routinely dropped by naive subsetting and load-bearing here.

settled.claim: China's public safety signage is a four-category colour-and-shape system, so the illocutionary force arrives before any character is decoded. GB 2894 《安全标志及其使用导则》: 禁止 (prohibition) = red circle with diagonal bar; 警告 (warning) = yellow equilateral triangle, black border; 指令 (mandatory) = blue filled circle; 提示 (notice) = green square. GB/T 10001 governs the public information pictograms. The emergency exit sign is green and reads 安全出口, not 出口 — 出口 on a blue or black plate is just the way out of the station.
settled.scope: GB 2894 is a mandatory GB standard; GB/T 10001 is a recommended one. The standard texts were not retrievable (openstd.samr.gov.cn 403-blocked) and the hex values given are approximations; the scheme itself is ISO 7010-aligned.
sources: GB 2894 《安全标志及其使用导则》 — https://openstd.samr.gov.cn/bzgk/gb/
GB/T 10001 《公共信息图形符号》
settled.implication: Teach the four categories first, with no characters at all — a two-bit classification plus a content lookup, learnable in about 90 seconds, in the highest-consequence situations. Render the real geometry at correct proportions and never recolour these to fit the app's chrome: the colour IS the content.

settled.claim: Transit is the LOWEST-payoff of the five domains and menus, supermarket labels and shopfronts are the highest, but the mechanism is observed practice, not a compliance rule. GB/T 30240 《公共服务领域英文译写规范》 is GB/T — 推荐性国家标准, RECOMMENDED and voluntary throughout — issued as Part 1 in 2013 and Parts 2-10 in 2017. The bilingualism of tier-1 metros, HSR stations and airports is real but driven by municipal procurement and Olympic/Expo-era practice. The sharper and correct version of the argument is the contrast with GB 7718, a MANDATORY standard that requires Chinese on food labels and caps foreign type size at no larger than the corresponding Chinese — so product labels are functionally Chinese-only. Shopfront fascias are unregulated for language and overwhelmingly Chinese-only outside tourist strips.
settled.scope: GB vs GB/T nomenclature is a high-confidence standards fact; the part list and issue dates were not verified (openstd.samr.gov.cn 403-blocked). The domain weights that follow have no empirical basis in encounter frequency — nobody has measured how many signs of each type a visitor needs to read per day.
sources: GB/T 30240 《公共服务领域英文译写规范》 — https://openstd.samr.gov.cn/bzgk/gb/
GB 7718 《食品安全国家标准 预包装食品标签通则》
settled.implication: Weight the category bag away from transit (market 30% / menu 30% / street 20% / safety 15% / transit 5%) and put a one-line justification in the app — 'the metro is already in English; the noodle shop is not' — because the ordering is counter-intuitive and players will otherwise think the bank is broken. Treat the weights as a v1 guess to be replaced by measured encounter rates.

settled.claim: Allergen declaration on Chinese packaged food has historically been RECOMMENDED (推荐性), not mandatory, under GB 7718-2011, for eight categories: 含麸质的谷物, 甲壳纲类动物, 鱼类, 蛋类, 花生, 大豆, 乳 (incl. 乳糖), 坚果. The absence of an allergen warning therefore carries no information. Nutrition labels under GB 28050 declare 能量 in kJ, not kcal — a factor of ~4.184 that silently misleads European readers.
settled.scope: A 2025 revision of GB 7718 moving allergen labelling toward mandatory, with a transition into 2027, is believed to exist but was NOT verified and must not be stated in the product until someone reads the standard.
sources: GB 7718-2011 《食品安全国家标准 预包装食品标签通则》 — https://openstd.samr.gov.cn/bzgk/gb/
GB 28050 《食品安全国家标准 预包装食品营养标签通则》
settled.implication: A player with a serious allergy must read the ingredient list itself, which is a much harder reading task than sign recognition. The app must state plainly, once, that it is a game and not a medical tool and that absence of a warning does not mean absence of the allergen. Do not let a game teach someone with a peanut allergy to trust a label.

settled.claim: The pinyin layer of the survival curriculum passes mechanical verification at 384/387 readings, including precisely the neutral-tone and heteronym choices where sloppy sources fail: 休息 xiūxi, 豆腐 dòufu, 馄饨 húntun, 芝麻 zhīma, 芥末 jièmo as neutral tones; 行 háng in 银行; 肚 dǔ for tripe; 美发 měifà; 炸 zhá for deep-fry; 干煸 gānbiān; 网吧 wǎngbā. All 14 asserted simplified/traditional pairs (检/檢, 续/續, 酱/醬, 咸/鹹, 饺/餃, 质/質, 药/藥, 摊/攤, 边/邊) verify under OpenCC.
settled.scope: All 387 readings run through pypinyin 0.55.0 with heteronym expansion. Three real errors found: 凤爪 is fèngzhǎo not fèngzhuǎ and 鸡爪 is jīzhǎo (爪 reads zhǎo in compounds, zhuǎ colloquially in 爪子); 'minded garlic' is a typo for 'minced garlic'; 里脊 is more standardly lǐji (neutral) than lǐjǐ.
sources: pypinyin 0.55.0 with heteronym expansion, run against all 387 readings this session
OpenCC s2t/t2s — https://github.com/BYVoid/OpenCC
settled.implication: Stop grading the lexical deliverable 'folklore'. The word lists are the strongest part of the corpus and are verified content, not received wisdom — the folklore label belongs on the unmeasured claims ABOUT them (encounter rates, HSK percentages, domain weights), not on the lexis. Apply the three corrections before content lock.

settled.claim: FSI puts Mandarin in Category IV ('super-hard'): 88 weeks / ~2,200 class hours to ILR 3/3, more than double Category III, for aptitude-screened full-time adult diplomats. ILR 3 ≈ CEFR C1 (General Professional Proficiency), not 'upper-B2/low-C1'. DLI runs Category IV Chinese at 64 weeks with a DLAB floor of 110 (not 111) and still sees substantial attrition.
settled.scope: These are institutional course-length policies, not research data: no published per-student variance, no confidence intervals, and nothing about the Dutch→Mandarin direction. The '64% DLPT success' figure the sweep quoted has no stated threshold or cohort and should be dropped.
sources: US Department of State, FSI School of Language Studies — Foreign Language Training — https://www.state.gov/national-foreign-affairs-training-center/foreign-language-training
13 FAH-1 H-220, Foreign Affairs Handbook — https://fam.state.gov/FAM/13FAH01/13FAH010220.html
Student Achievement Indicators at DLIFLC, US Army Research Institute AD1150437 — https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/trecms/pdf/AD1150437.pdf
settled.implication: Do not scope the product as 'learn Mandarin' and never set the in-app goal metric to a CEFR or HSK level. Architect for churn as the primary failure mode: a three-week gap must not reset progress, and the first re-entry after a lapse should be a 60-second 'what you still know' review built from the player's own scheduler state.

settled.claim: There is a ready-made, officially-defined 400-character tier for the Dutch market: Chinese is a VWO exam subject examined only as a schoolexamen (no centraal examen), with PTA tests structurally based on HSK, requiring active mastery of 400 characters.
settled.scope: slo.nl was egress-blocked. The start year is unresolved (2015-16 vs per 1 August 2017 with first exams 2018-19) and the per-skill CEFR targets are unverified. The 400-character figure and the schoolexamen-only structure are the load-bearing parts and are confirmed by multiple secondary sources — one email to SLO settles all of it.
sources: SLO — Chinees vwo — https://www.slo.nl/sectoren/havo-vwo/chinees-vwo/
SLO — Chinees op school: voorstel voor een leerplan Chinees — https://www.slo.nl/publish/pages/4250/chinees-op-school_webversie.pdf
settled.implication: Tag every item vwo_400 and hsk3_band and offer Dutch secondary students a filtered deck. Two columns for a distribution wedge into a small, enumerable list of Dutch schools.

contested.question: Does handwriting practice help or hurt L2 character RECOGNITION?
contested.side_a: Process view: hold exposure to the character constant and vary the encoding process, and writing wins. Guan, Liu, Chan, Ye & Perfetti (2011, JEP 103(3):509-522, N=48, five consecutive days): handwriting group better on form recognition and character-meaning; pinyin-typing group better on character-phonology. Xu, Chang, Zhang & Perfetti (2013, Foreign Language Annals) replicated the writing advantage for form recognition.
contested.side_b: Opportunity-cost view: hold total instructional TIME constant and vary the activity, and writing loses. Lu, Ostrow & Heffernan (2019, AERA Open 5(4)), a registered-report replication run inside ASSISTments: learners who spent 30% of practice time hand-copying scored significantly LOWER on word-recognition posttests at immediate, 1-day and 1-week, with no compensating gain on the on-paper posttests.
contested.what_it_turns_on: The two literatures are not testing the same question, and no registered replication runs both manipulations in one design. Chai & Ma (2022, Frontiers 12:779190, HSK data from 74,362 CSL learners across 67 L1s) is observational and cannot separate writing skill from total effort. The fMRI evidence sometimes cited for side A ('handwriting produced stronger bilateral superior parietal and right postcentral activation than pinyin typing') is reverse inference and establishes nothing about learning — writing with your hand should activate sensorimotor cortex more regardless. Practical resolution: for a three-week trip with recognition as the criterion task, side B governs — but this is a considered trade, not a free choice, and the product should say so.
sources: Guan, C. Q. et al. (2011). Journal of Educational Psychology 103(3):509-522 — NOTE the sweep's URL for this paper is wrong: it carries csl.00033.zha, which is Zhang (2024)'s Benjamins DOI. Repair before use.
Lu, X., Ostrow, K. S. & Heffernan, N. T. (2019). Save Your Strokes. AERA Open 5(4) — https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1238487
Chai, X. & Ma, M. (2022). Frontiers in Psychology 12:779190 — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8900728/

contested.question: Should the low-scaffold tier show pinyin or a semantic-component hint?
contested.side_a: Swap pinyin for a component hint: Guan et al. (2011) shows pinyin coding strengthens phonology while the orthographic route is what character recognition depends on, so a pinyin crutch on a READING product makes the item easier in a way that does not build the needed representation. A Dutch player reads 'chū kǒu', feels supported, and learns a sound they will never need to produce.
contested.side_b: The inference overreaches the study. Guan et al. compared handwriting against alphabetic coding — a dissociation, not evidence that a pinyin HINT at test time harms reading, and neither contrast was run. There is a live counter-literature in which pinyin/phonological knowledge positively predicts Chinese character reading in L2 learners, and highly experienced learners activate character orthography when reading pinyin, which argues against pinyin being a competing representation. The product also wants phonology anyway — it ships a 'point at this' screen so the player can say 不要香菜.
contested.what_it_turns_on: Whether a scaffold present only at study time and absent at the transfer target is neutral or harmful. Nobody has run the contrast. Better citations for the thing actually wanted (that explicit semantic-radical instruction aids character learning) are Shen & Ke (2007) and Taft & Chung (1999), not Guan et al., which is a handwriting paper. Ship the component-hint swap as a good product hypothesis with an A/B test attached, graded weak — not as evidence-backed.
sources: Guan, C. Q. et al. (2011). Journal of Educational Psychology 103(3)
