Shen, H. H. & Ke, C. (2007). Radical awareness and word acquisition among nonnative learners of Chinese. Modern Language Journal 91(1):97-111
Taft, M. & Chung, K. (1999). Using radicals in teaching Chinese characters to second language learners. Psychologia 42 — suggested, not verified
Reading Pinyin activates character orthography for highly experienced learners of Chinese. Bilingualism: Language and Cognition

contested.question: Does rendering each item as the physical object it appears on help or install a false skill?
contested.side_a: Real risk of logo-reading. Masonheimer, Drum & Ehri (1984, Journal of Reading Behavior 16(4):257-271, n=102): children who confidently 'read' familiar environmental print largely failed to notice an altered letter (XEPSI for PEPSI), and their environmental-print skill did not predict decontextualised word reading — the whole visual gestalt is the cue, not the letters. Applied here: a learner who has only met 出口 in enamel-blue Beijing-metro styling may be recognising the plate, and may fail on 出 in 出发, 出租, 出售, 支出.
contested.side_b: The memory case for realism is weak but the non-memory case is strong. Smith & Vela (2001, Psychonomic Bulletin & Review 8(2):203-220, meta-analysis of ~75 studies) find environmental context-dependent memory reliable but modest and attenuated by outshining; Godden & Baddeley found a substantial context effect for free RECALL (1975) and essentially none for RECOGNITION (1980) — and this product is recognition throughout. But typeface class is the part that genuinely varies in the wild, CTW needs a 'wordart' annotation class for decorative lettering, and realism buys motivation and object recognition, which is half of real reading.
contested.what_it_turns_on: Whether transfer is forced. The design response is not to abandon realism but to require it to generalise: multiple treatments per character, a naked probe, and a measured gap. Neumann et al. (2011) report mixed or null incremental effects for environmental print once general print knowledge is controlled, so this is a genuine risk, not a settled result. It is the most expensive part of the design and the evidence is contested — instrument it from v1.
sources: Masonheimer, P. E., Drum, P. A. & Ehri, L. C. (1984). Journal of Reading Behavior 16(4):257-271 — https://doi.org/10.1080/10862968409547521
Smith, S. M. & Vela, E. (2001). Psychonomic Bulletin & Review 8(2):203-220 — https://doi.org/10.3758/BF03196157
Godden, D. R. & Baddeley, A. D. (1975; 1980). British Journal of Psychology 66(3); 71(1)
Neumann, M. M. et al. (2011). Journal of Early Childhood Literacy — https://doi.org/10.1177/1468798411417080

contested.question: Is there a lexical coverage THRESHOLD (95%/98%) at all?
contested.side_a: Threshold view: Hu & Nation (2000, RFL 13(1), n=66) found ~98% coverage needed for unassisted comprehension of fiction with 95% giving only partial comprehension; Laufer & Ravenhorst-Kalovski (2010) position 95% as minimal and 98% as optimal; Kremmel et al. (2023, Language Learning) report a direct replication.
contested.side_b: No-breakpoint view: Schmitt, Jiang & Grabe (2011, Modern Language Journal 95(1):26-43) tested explicitly for a breakpoint on a large sample and reported a broadly linear relationship with no distinct threshold. One Chinese-context study testing seven coverage levels (90-100%) found no clean threshold either.
contested.what_it_turns_on: Whether comprehension is a step function of coverage or a smooth one. Either way the numbers are word-token based, derived from running text in English-L2 research, and there is NO established character-level threshold for L2 Chinese. This makes the product's conclusion stronger, not weaker: if there is no breakpoint even in redundant running text, importing 95%/98% into a domain with no redundancy at all is doubly unjustified. 保质期12个月 is four content characters; missing 质 or 期 loses the whole message.
sources: Hu, M. & Nation, I. S. P. (2000). Reading in a Foreign Language 13(1):403-430 — not retrieved
Schmitt, N., Jiang, X. & Grabe, W. (2011). Modern Language Journal 95(1):26-43 — not retrieved; verify before use
Kremmel, B. et al. (2023). Unknown Vocabulary Density and Reading Comprehension: Replicating Hu and Nation (2000). Language Learning
Shen, M. et al. (2025). Language, Culture and Curriculum 39(1) — CSL textbook series reaches only 81% word-token coverage by its final volume

contested.question: Should a Dutch adult fluent in English get Dutch or English glosses?
contested.side_a: Dutch (L1). Two glossing meta-analyses agree L1 > L2, with the advantage clearest for beginners — exactly this population.
contested.side_b: English (L2). The L2 Status Factor (Bardel & Falk) predicts English would be the privileged transfer source because of shared late-learned metalinguistic status; and Chen (2025, TESOL Quarterly) reports both gloss languages at medium effect and argues learner preference can decide.
contested.what_it_turns_on: There is no study of Dutch–English bilinguals learning Mandarin, and the L3 theory cuts both ways: the Typological Primacy Model predicts transfer follows psychotypological proximity, and Mandarin is remote from both Dutch and English, which drains the L3 argument for English entirely. The L1 advantage is also small (g ≈ 0.33) and measured on glosses met while reading connected text, which this product does not have. This is the weakest link in the cluster and the highest-value thing to settle with the product's own A/B data. For a concrete-referent domain (menus, signage) the picture-gloss decision probably matters more than the language decision.
sources: Kim, H. S., Lee, J. H. & Lee, H. Language Teaching Research — https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/full/10.1177/1362168820981394
Rothman, J. (2011). Typological Primacy Model. Second Language Research — https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1177/0267658310386439
Chen, X. (2025). TESOL Quarterly — https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/tesq.3394

contested.question: Does high-variability phonetic training with many talkers beat low-variability training, and does the app need an audio channel at all?
contested.side_a: HVPT works with large effects: two independent meta-analyses (79 studies, g = 0.92 pretest-posttest / g = 0.67 treatment-control; and 18 studies, g = 0.77 overall) with a LARGE effect specifically for lexical tone, and five-to-eight talkers giving g = 0.77 versus g = 0.55 for two-to-four. The canonical Mandarin protocol is ~8 sessions over 2 weeks with trial-by-trial feedback, yielding ~21% perception gain that generalises to new talkers and survives 6 months.
contested.side_b: The variability component itself is contested — controlled comparisons have found high-variability training does not reliably beat low-variability training for non-native contrasts, sometimes helping only higher-aptitude learners. The identification-over-discrimination gap (g = 0.95 vs 0.57) is a between-study moderator confounded with test format (identification testing g = 1.08 vs discrimination testing g = 0.77), not an experimental manipulation. And the canonical protocol rests on an n=8 original study generalised via a meta-analysis of the paradigm, not a dose-response trial. '4-6 talkers' is invented precision.
contested.what_it_turns_on: A prior scope question the sweeps never resolved: real Chinese signage carries no pinyin and no audio, so for a reading-only product the sibilant contrast, the talker rotation and the pitch-contour pre-test all train a channel that is absent at the transfer target. The cost is concrete — ~900 items × 5 talkers × ~30 KB Opus ≈ 135 MB, on top of ~900 photographs at two resolutions, into a PWA cache, offline, in China. The current design buys both and budgets neither.
sources: Uchihara, T., Karas, M. & Thomson, R. I. (2025). High variability phonetic training (HVPT): A meta-analysis. SSLA
Mahdi, H. S. & Mohsen, M. A. (2024). Language Teaching Research Quarterly 40:29-45 — https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/EJ1425175.pdf
Wang, Y., Spence, M. M., Jongman, A. & Sereno, J. A. (1999). JASA 106(6):3649-3658
Brekelmans, G. et al. — controlled comparison finding no reliable HV-over-LV advantage; cited from knowledge, unverifiable

contested.question: What optimal spacing gap should a trip-anchored scheduler use?
contested.side_a: A flat 10-20% of the retention interval, giving gapDays = clamp(0.15 × daysUntil(tripEnd), 0.5, 14) — so ~2-4 days for a 21-day horizon and ~12 hours for a 5-day horizon.
contested.side_b: Cepeda et al.'s 'temporal ridgeline' result is precisely that the optimal gap as a PROPORTION of the retention interval DECLINES as the interval lengthens: roughly RI 7d → gap ~1d (~14%), RI 35d → ~11d (~31%), RI 70d → ~21d (~30%), RI 350d → ~21d (~6%). At this product's target horizon (~21-35 days) the empirical points sit nearer 25-30%, i.e. gaps of ~5-9 days, not 2-4.
contested.what_it_turns_on: Also a design-transfer question: Cepeda et al. (2008) is a TWO-SESSION paradigm — one study, one restudy, one gap — and generalising a single-gap optimum to a multi-review adaptive scheduler is an extrapolation the paper does not license. Keep the trip-anchored idea (it is genuinely novel and correct in spirit), use a coefficient nearer 0.25-0.30 for 2-6 week horizons, floor it well above 0.5 days, and A/B two coefficients against landing-day retention — nobody in the literature has done that. The asymmetry claim (short gaps penalised more steeply than long ones) is the part worth keeping.
sources: Cepeda, N. J., Vul, E., Rohrer, D., Wixted, J. T. & Pashler, H. (2008). Psychological Science 19(11):1095-1102 — not retrieved; verify the gap/RI table before implementing
Cepeda, N. J. et al. (2006). Psychological Bulletin 132(3):354-380 — 254 studies, 839 comparisons, 14,594 participants

contested.question: Does the testing effect's pooled g ≈ 0.50 apply to a four-option recognition design?
contested.side_a: Rowland (2014, 159 effect sizes) puts testing over restudy at g ≈ 0.50, cited to justify both the main format and converting spectator exposure into spectator retrieval.
contested.side_b: That meta-analysis is well known for finding the effect strongly MODERATED by test format — largest for free recall, smaller for cued recall, smallest for recognition — and by feedback. Four-option multiple choice IS recognition, so the pooled number is being quoted to justify a design sitting in the weakest cell of the very moderator analysis it cites.
contested.what_it_turns_on: The transfer-appropriate-processing defence of multiple choice survives on its own terms — reading a sign in the wild IS constrained recognition against the small set of things that sign could plausibly say — so keep the format for the main game and stop attaching a pooled number to it. But the spectator/shadow task should NOT be another 4-option tap: make it production or cued recall ('what does this sign make you DO?', no options shown), same interaction cost, strongest rather than weakest moderator cell. Separately, a 4-option format has a 25% guess floor and systematically overestimates the cued-recall knowledge that reading an unaided sign requires.
sources: Rowland, C. A. (2014). Psychological Bulletin 140(6):1432-1463 — not retrieved; verify subgroup estimates before quoting
Morris, C. D., Bransford, J. D. & Franks, J. J. (1977). Journal of Verbal Learning and Verbal Behavior 16(5):519-533

Little, J. L. & Bjork, E. L. (2015). Memory & Cognition 43(1):14-26 — competitive plausible alternatives produce retention benefits for the tested item AND for information related to the incorrect alternatives

myths.myth: 'There is no published character-frequency corpus of Chinese urban signage, so the item bank cannot be corpus-derived and we must build one by peer-to-peer photo capture.'
myths.why_wrong: False, and it was the load-bearing negative finding of the whole curriculum sweep. CTW (Chinese Text in the Wild, Tsinghua/Tencent, JCST 2019) has 1,018,402 individually character-labelled instances over 32,285 street-view images and 3,850 characters, freely downloadable, with a stat_frequency step already in the shipped baseline. The sweep searched the linguistic-landscape literature — the wrong field; this lives in computer vision. The stated success metric for the capture feature ('after ~5,000 captures you own the dataset nobody has published') is false on both halves: the dataset is published, and 5,000 captures is a rounding error against 1M labelled instances.
sources: Yuan et al. (2019). A Large Chinese Text Dataset in the Wild. JCST 34(3):509-521 — https://ctwdataset.github.io/
https://github.com/yuantailing/ctw-baseline

myths.myth: '~80-85% of Chinese characters are semantic-phonetic compounds, so component decomposition is the dominant regularity and a pictograph path covers under 10% of the script.'
myths.why_wrong: Unit-of-analysis error. That is a whole-script statistic and this product's bank is the head of the frequency distribution, where transparency is inversely related to frequency. In the top 1,000 only ~53% are phonetic compounds and ~47% are pictographs or ideographs; in the first 100 it is ~29% vs ~71%; in the literal first 50 characters only 12/50 are pictophonetic. Pictographs alone are 3.6× enriched in the top 1,000 (9.1%) relative to the whole script (2.5%).
sources: Computed over makemeahanzi (n=9,574) × jieba-derived frequency ranking — https://github.com/skishore/makemeahanzi
Shu et al. (2003), Child Development 74(1) — the source of the whole-script figure, abstract-only

myths.myth: 'A single two-slot card — left box = meaning, right box = sound — handles ~72% of the bank.'
myths.why_wrong: Two errors compounding. The 72% is 72% OF PHONOGRAMS, not of all characters; left-right structure is 44.8% of the top 1,000 and 30.0% of the top 100. And the layout is only semantically honest for characters that are BOTH left-right AND phonetic — 30.7% of the top 1,000 and 13.0% of the top 100. As a default card it would teach a false analysis of 一 是 人 了 不 中 国 大 and every ideograph, i.e. of roughly 70-87% of the earliest items.
sources: Computed: makemeahanzi decomposition × 通用规范汉字表 Tier 1 (verified at exactly 3,500 characters)
Hsiao & Shillcock (2006), J. Psycholinguistic Research 35 — the misapplied source

myths.myth: 'Budget for about 1 in 3 phonetic hints being wrong.'
myths.why_wrong: Roughly 2× too optimistic for the band the product ships. Over the top 1,000, a phonetic component predicts the full reading including tone only ~17% of the time and gives NO cue at all ~35% of the time — about 5 in 6 are wrong at tone level. Reliability roughly doubles by the full dictionary (~34% exact), so the feature is worth more at intermediate than at beginner level.
sources: Computed: makemeahanzi etymology.phonetic × Unihan readings (mozillazg/pinyin-data)
The sweep's own citation for the 26%/39% figures links to the Wikipedia biography of Zhou Youguang, which cannot source them

myths.myth: 'HSK band order is not frequency order — a travel-reading player needs 出口 and 元 before HSK would give them.'
myths.why_wrong: The illustrative example is refuted by the HSK list itself: 出 (rank 26), 口 (rank 157) and 元 (rank 211) are ALL HSK 1. HSK band order IS strongly frequency-aligned (median rank rises monotonically 291→2,637), band sizes are 125-441 rather than '~300', and HSK BEATS raw frequency on this product's vocabulary — 厕 is frequency rank 3,107 but sits in HSK 4.
sources: Computed: HSK 3.0 hanzi lists — https://github.com/krmanik/HSK-3.0 × jieba-derived frequency

myths.myth: 'Teach 月 = flesh/body-part and highlight it inside 肠 肚 肝 肺 肾 腰 脑.'
myths.why_wrong: Wrong codepoint, and it ships as a silent bug. The component is ⺼ (U+2EBC, Kangxi 130 meat), not 月 (U+6708, moon) — homoglyphs in almost every font. A string match on 月 highlights ZERO of the six targets and fires instead on 期, which sits inside 保质期, a Tier-1 item. Independently verified here. The exception list was also wrong twice: 舌 was omitted (it does not carry the component), and 筋 does carry it inside 肋 but takes ⺮ as its Kangxi radical. And even the general gloss misfires: 月 as moon or a graphic merger appears in 期 朗 服 有 望.
sources: Verified this session against makemeahanzi radical/decomposition fields — https://github.com/skishore/makemeahanzi
Unicode U+2EBC KANGXI RADICAL MEAT vs U+6708

myths.myth: 'Ship a ~30-radical onboarding module including 食 as the food radical, plus 男 and 页.'
myths.why_wrong: Three content errors. 食 is the wrong simplified form: the productive left-hand food radical is 饣, taken by 43 common characters (饭 饿 馆 饺 饼 饮 馒 饥 饱 …) versus 12 for 食, mostly traditional or rare — a learner taught 食 will not recognise it in 饭馆 or 饺子. 男 is not a radical at all (it is 田 + 力 and is indexed under one of those). 页 (from 頁, head) yields 顶 顺 须 顾 颈 项 领 颜 额 题 — essentially zero menu or signage payoff. Meanwhile the highest-value menu radical is missing entirely: 火/灬 is the radical of 9 of the 13 core cooking methods.
sources: Verified this session: makemeahanzi radical counts — 饣 43, 食 12, 火 128, 灬 28, 刂 71, 阝 160
Kangxi radical index: 男 is not among the 214 radicals; 页/頁 is radical 181

myths.myth: Tone colour-coding on characters.
myths.why_wrong: Unevidenced folklore that is also the default in most competing apps. No controlled trial of Mandarin tone colour coding could be located; the schemes are mutually incompatible across Pleco, Hanping, Skritter and Dong Chinese. It contradicts the direct finding that added colour on the glyph raises reaction times and lowers accuracy, it builds a crutch with no transfer target (real signage carries no colour-coded tone), and colour-only encoding is a WCAG 1.4.1 failure — the common four-tone palettes are red/green/blue/purple, and red-green is the failing pair for ~8% of males.
sources: Hou, F. & Jiang, X. (2022). Frontiers in Psychology 13:783613
Li, J., Shi, M. & Wang, X. (2025). Languages 10(10):260
W3C WCAG 2.2, SC 1.4.1 Use of Color (Level A)

myths.myth: 'Early pinyin creates dependence and harms character acquisition (the pinyin crutch).'
myths.why_wrong: No adequately powered RCT of pinyin-first vs character-first exists. The empirical evidence that could be located points the other way — pinyin ability and pinyin study time were not correlated with character recognition in beginners, and highly experienced learners activate character orthography when READING pinyin, which argues against pinyin being a competing representation. Practitioner assertion, not measurement. (The separate, better-supported point is about PLACEMENT, not presence: pinyin adjacent and per-character beats pinyin trailing the string.)
sources: Reading Pinyin activates character orthography for highly experienced learners of Chinese. Bilingualism: Language and Cognition
Lee, C. H. & Kalyuga, S. (2011). Language Learning 61(4):1099-1118

myths.myth: Heisig-style, Mandarin Blueprint-style and Chineasy character systems as validated methods.
myths.why_wrong: No peer-reviewed trial of Remembering the Simplified/Traditional Hanzi, Mandarin Blueprint or Chineasy exists; all located evaluations are practitioner reviews. Zhang (2024)'s systematic review of 22 articles and 39 methods contains no trial of any of them. For Chineasy the structural objection is decisive and quantitative — pictographs are ~8-10% of the script, so a pictograph-based system cannot scale — and Victor Mair's Language Log critique quotes a US university Chinese program director saying 'what she is teaching is not reading'. Repeating Chineasy-style false etymologies is a known reputational liability among Chinese-teaching professionals.
sources: Mair, V. (2014). Chineasy? Not. Language Log — https://languagelog.ldc.upenn.edu/nll/?p=11109
Zhang, S. (2024). Chinese as a Second Language — https://benjamins.com/catalog/csl.00033.zha

myths.myth: 'Imagery mnemonics beat rote for Chinese characters.'
myths.why_wrong: The classic finding is the opposite of the marketing claim. Wang & Thomas (1992, Language Learning 42(3)): across two 2×2 studies on English translations of Chinese characters, experimenter-supplied imagery mnemonics showed NO advantage beyond the immediate test and produced GREATER forgetting at 2-day and 1-week delays. The authors attribute this to experimenter-imposed versus subject-generated encoding — which predicts that LEARNER-generated mnemonics may behave differently, and is the only version worth shipping. Separately, the keyword method's meta-analytic support links an L2 SOUND to an L1 word, so it addresses pinyin-to-meaning, not glyph-to-meaning, and does not transfer to character recognition at all.
sources: Wang, A. Y. & Thomas, M. H. (1992). Language Learning 42(3) — https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ451687
Pressley, M., Levin, J. R. & Delaney, H. D. (1982). Review of Educational Research 52(1):61-91

myths.myth: '~83% of game-using learners outperformed non-users' (and mobile-game effect sizes of g ≈ 0.96-1.28 as planning constants).
myths.why_wrong: The 83% is not an observed proportion. It is Cohen's U3, mechanically derived from g = 0.962 under normality and equal variance (Φ(0.962) ≈ 0.83) — a distributional conversion reported as a headcount of people. Delete the sentence. The magnitudes are also not credible as causal estimates: in education RCTs the median effect is ~0.10 SD and 0.30 SD is large, so effects near 1.0 SD signal researcher-made outcome measures aligned to the treatment, small quasi-experimental samples, no active control, and publication bias. The '10 weeks' moderator is dose, not calendar shape — nothing says effects 'reach' g = 1.28 at week 10.
sources: Kraft, M. A. (2020). Interpreting Effect Sizes of Education Interventions. Educational Researcher 49(4)
Cohen's U3 identity: Φ(0.962) ≈ 0.83 — arithmetic
Sailer & Homner (2020). Educational Psychology Review 32 — small pooled effects, high heterogeneity

myths.myth: 'Advanced Dutch learners show strongest sensitivity to T1 and weakest to T4.'
myths.why_wrong: Runs against essentially the whole Mandarin tone-perception literature. T4 (high-falling) has the steepest, most salient F0 excursion and is consistently among the BEST-identified tones by non-tonal-L1 learners — including in Hao (2012), cited approvingly two findings earlier in the same sweep. If the paradigm was contrast-based (T1-T2, T2-T3, T3-T4), 'sensitivity to T1' is not even a well-formed unit of that design. Quarantine it: probably reversed or mis-transcribed from an abstract. The safe, literature-consistent prior is T4 among the easiest and T2/T3 the hardest.
sources: Hao, Y.-C. (2012). Journal of Phonetics 40(2)
Zou, Caspers & Chen (2022). Frontiers in Psychology 13:891756 — results section must be read before any design keys off this

myths.myth: 'Musicians learn tone better, so ask about instruments in onboarding.'
myths.why_wrong: The original finding is real but correlational. Schellenberg & Lima (2024, Annual Review of Psychology) conclude that replication attempts frequently fail, that experimental and longitudinal studies report small or mixed effects, and that music-training associations disappear when music APTITUDE is held constant — selection, not transfer. Do not branch content on it and do not spend an onboarding slot. If an adaptive signal is wanted, use the thing that actually predicted learning: a 60-second, 12-trial pre-test of pitch-contour identification on NON-SPEECH tones.
sources: Wong, P. C. M. & Perrachione, T. K. (2007). Applied Psycholinguistics 28(4)
Schellenberg, E. G. & Lima, C. F. (2024). Music Training and Nonmusical Abilities. Annual Review of Psychology — https://www.annualreviews.org/doi/10.1146/annurev-psych-032323-051354

myths.myth: Assorted content errors that would ship as wrong teaching or wrong copy.
myths.why_wrong: (1) '注意, 休息 and 医院 are absent from HSK 1-3' — 注意 is HSK 2.0 L3, 休息 is L2, 医院 is L1. (2) '檢 續 醬 鹹 餃 質 藥 攤 邊 are dense simplified characters' — those are TRADITIONAL forms; the simplified equivalents are 检 11, 续 11, 酱 13, 咸 9, 饺 9, 质 8, 药 9, 摊 13, 边 5. (3) '无座 is the same price as a hard seat' — true on conventional trains, but on G/D high-speed services 无座 is sold at the 二等座 fare. (4) '凤爪 fèngzhuǎ' — it is fèngzhǎo, and 鸡爪 is jīzhǎo. (5) '蒜蓉 — minded garlic' — minced. (6) 'GB/T 30240 standardised English translations' as if compulsory — GB/T is 推荐性, recommended and voluntary; Part 1 issued 2013, Parts 2-10 in 2017. (7) '-ün is an elided-vowel rime' — -ün is not a pinyin spelling at all (the umlaut is dropped after j/q/x/y), and jun/qun/xun/yun is /yn/ with NO elided vowel; expanding it would teach jūn as ⟨ju-en⟩. The real elided set is exactly -iu /jou̯/, -ui /wei̯/ and -un /wən/ after a NON-palatal initial. (8) 'HSK study-hour tables (80-150 h for HSK 1, 500-1,000 h for HSK 4)' — no official hour table exists for HSK 3.0; these are unsourced planning estimates. (9) 'A lint rule rejecting items with a verb and no overt subject' — it would reject 禁止吸烟, 小心地滑, 请勿触摸 and 卖完了 and empty the bank.
sources: HSK 2.0 official lists parsed this session — https://github.com/glxxyz/hskhsk.com
Stroke counts verified against makemeahanzi graphics.txt; simplified/traditional pairs via OpenCC
pypinyin 0.55.0 heteronym expansion over all 387 readings
Standard Hanyu Pinyin orthography (GB/T 16159) — ü-dropping after j/q/x/y is a spelling rule

directives.directive: TIER 0 — the first session: ~24 items, linear, unskippable, single-player, no betting, no timer, high scaffolding, ~12 minutes, running BEFORE multiplayer is available. Order: (1) the GB 2894 four-colour safety system, no characters shown. (2) 男/女 as a pair. (3) 出口/入口 as a pair, plus 安全出口 in green. (4) 推/拉 as a pair. (5) 禁止 and 请勿 as the two prohibition openers. (6) 小心 and 危险. (7) 营业中/休息. (8) 元 and 块. (9) 斤 with the 500 g arithmetic. (10) 辣 and 麻辣. (11) 肉 = pork. (12) 素 vs 荤. (13) 洗手间/厕所. (14) 满/空. The 60-character Tier-0 inventory: 出入口男女禁止小心危险开关推拉上下大小前后内外满空免费收费营业休息元角分斤克特价折满减号线站换乘辣麻素荤生冷热.
directives.basis: Practitioner-derived ordering; every item is behaviour-changing and several prevent harm. Solves the co-located cold-start problem (four players of wildly different levels) by guaranteeing a shared floor. The ordering is unmeasured — 荤 stays in Tier 0 on consequence grounds despite falling outside the official 3,000-character standard.

directives.directive:
MENU STRAND 1 — cooking methods, item-bank rank 1-13 of the menu strand, BEFORE proteins. Format: 汉字 pīnyīn — English / Nederlands — what it predicts.
Core 13: 炒 chǎo — stir-fry / roerbakken — fast, wok, moderate oil. 爆 bào — flash-fry / flitsbakken — very high heat, seconds, often offal. 炸 zhá — deep-fry / frituren — heavy oil. 煮 zhǔ — boil / koken — plain, wet. 蒸 zhēng — steam / stomen — lightest, no added oil. 烤 kǎo — roast, grill, bake / roosteren, grillen — dry heat, often skewers. 焖 mèn — covered braise / smoren — lid on, tender, saucy. 炖 dùn — long stew / stoven — soupy, bones, hours. 涮 shuàn — swish in broth / kort dompelen — this is hotpot, you cook it yourself. 拌 bàn — tossed, dressed / aanmaken — almost always COLD, raw or blanched, vinegar+oil. 卤 lǔ — master-stock braise / in kruidenbouillon gegaard — dark, star anise, usually served cold, usually offal. 烧 shāo — braise / braiseren — soy and sugar, thick sauce. 煎 jiān — pan-fry / bakken in de pan — shallow oil, one side crisp.
Compound modifiers that override the method: 红烧 hóngshāo — red-braised / in sojasaus gestoofd — sweet-savoury, brown, mild, the safest thing on any menu. 清蒸 qīngzhēng — plain-steamed / puur gestoomd — mild. 清炒 qīngchǎo — plain stir-fried / puur geroerbakt — mild. 白灼 báizhuó — blanched, Cantonese / geblancheerd — mild. 糖醋 tángcù — sweet and sour / zoetzuur — mild. 干煸 gānbiān — dry-fried / drooggebakken — Sichuan, chilli-heavy. 干锅 gānguō — dry pot / droge pan — Sichuan, arrives on a burner, chilli-heavy. 水煮 shuǐzhǔ — 'water-boiled' / letterlijk 'in water gekookt' — A LIE: a pool of chilli oil and Sichuan pepper; 水煮鱼 and 水煮肉片 are among the hottest dishes commonly ordered by mistake.
Secondary: 熘/溜 liū — thickened stir-fry. 烩 huì — thick stew. 焗 jú — baked, Cantonese. 熏 xūn — smoked / gerookt. 腌 yān — cured, pickled / gepekeld. 醉 zuì — wine-cured, RAW / rauw in wijn. 生腌 shēngyān — raw-marinated seafood / rauw gemarineerd — food-safety flag for visitors.
Tag each with heatLevel, oilLevel, servedTemp so consequence questions generate procedurally ('you are avoiding oil — which of these four dishes?'). Give 水煮, 干煸, 干锅 the hazard-board template, not the menu template.
directives.basis: Pinyin mechanically verified (384/387 across the whole deliverable, and 干煸 gānbiān and 炸 zhá are exactly the readings sloppy sources get wrong). HSK absence MEASURED: every one of 炒炸煮蒸烤焖炖涮拌卤烧煎爆 is outside HSK 3.0's first 900 characters. 火/灬 is the radical of 9 of these 13 (炒爆炸煮烤焖炖烧煎), verified this session — so one radical card unlocks most of the strand.

directives.directive:
MENU STRAND 2 — proteins and staples. 肉 alone on a Chinese menu means PORK by default.
Proteins: 肉 ròu — meat, and by default PORK / vlees, standaard VARKENSVLEES — 肉丝, 肉片, 肉末 with no animal named are all pork. 猪 zhū — pig / varken. 鸡 jī — chicken / kip. 牛 niú — beef / rund. 羊 yáng — lamb, mutton, goat / lam, schaap, geit. 鱼 yú — fish / vis. 虾 xiā — shrimp, prawn / garnaal. 蟹 xiè — crab / krab. 鸭 yā — duck / eend. 蛋 dàn — egg / ei. 鹅 é — goose / gans. 兔 tù — rabbit / konijn. 鸽 gē — pigeon / duif. 驴 lǘ — donkey / ezel. 鱿鱼 yóuyú — squid / inktvis. 贝 bèi — shellfish / schelpdier. 蛤蜊 / 花甲 gélí / huājiǎ — clam / venusschelp. 扇贝 shànbèi — scallop / sint-jakobsschelp. 生蚝 / 牡蛎 shēngháo / mǔlì — oyster / oester. 小龙虾 xiǎolóngxiā — crayfish / rivierkreeft. 排骨 páigǔ — ribs / spareribs. 五花肉 wǔhuāròu — pork belly / buikspek. 牛腩 niúnǎn — brisket / runderborst. 里脊 lǐji — tenderloin / haas. 豆腐 dòufu — tofu / tofu. 腐竹 fǔzhú — tofu skin / tofuvel. 面筋 miànjīn — seitan / seitan.
Staples: 饭 fàn — cooked rice, also 'meal' / rijst, maaltijd. 米饭 mǐfàn — steamed rice / gestoomde rijst. 炒饭 chǎofàn — fried rice / gebakken rijst. 面 miàn — wheat noodles, also 'flour' / tarwenoedels. 面条 miàntiáo — noodles / noedels. 拉面 lāmiàn — hand-pulled / handgetrokken noedels. 刀削面 dāoxiāomiàn — knife-shaved / geschaafde noedels. 粉 fěn — rice noodles or powder / rijstnoedels. 米粉 mǐfěn — rice vermicelli / rijstvermicelli. 河粉 héfěn — flat rice noodles / brede rijstnoedels. 粉丝 fěnsī — glass noodles / glasnoedels. 饺 jiǎo — dumpling / dumpling — 水饺 boiled / gekookt, 蒸饺 steamed / gestoomd, 煎饺 pan-fried / gebakken. 包 bāo — filled steamed bun / gevuld gestoomd broodje — 包子, 小笼包. 馒头 mántou — plain steamed bun, unfilled / ongevuld gestoomd broodje. 汤 tāng — soup / soep. 粥 zhōu — congee / rijstepap. 菜 cài — dish, or vegetable / gerecht, groente. 饼 bǐng — flatbread, pancake / platbrood, pannenkoek. 串 chuàn — skewer / spies. 锅 guō — pot / pan — 火锅 hotpot, 砂锅 clay pot. 馄饨 / 云吞 / 抄手 húntun / yúntūn / chāoshǒu — wonton, three regional names for the same thing / wonton, drie regionale namen. 油条 yóutiáo — fried dough stick / gefrituurd deegstokje.
Dish-name traps containing no such animal: 鱼香 yúxiāng — 'fish-fragrant', contains no fish / bevat geen vis. 蚂蚁上树 mǎyǐ shàng shù — 'ants climbing a tree', minced pork with glass noodles / geen mieren. 狮子头 shīzitóu — 'lion's head', a pork meatball / varkensgehaktbal. 夫妻肺片 fūqī fèipiàn — cold sliced beef offal, no lung nowadays / koude runderorgaanplakjes. 蚝油 háoyóu — oyster sauce, hides in 'vegetarian' dishes / oestersaus, zit vaak in 'vegetarische' gerechten. 高汤 gāotāng — meat stock / vleesbouillon.
directives.basis: Pinyin mechanically verified; 里脊 corrected from lǐjǐ to the more standard neutral lǐji. 肉=pork is not taught by any HSK level and catches vegetarians, Muslims and Jews daily. 馄饨 húntun and 豆腐 dòufu neutral tones verified correct.

directives.directive:
MENU STRAND 3 — flavour, heat dialling, and the organ/texture set. 麻 is not 'spicy' and has no Dutch or English word.
Flavour: 辣 là — chilli-hot / pittig, heet. 麻 má — the numbing, buzzing, lip-tingling effect of Sichuan pepper 花椒 / verdovend, tintelend — NOT heat, NOT spicy; 'pittig' is wrong. 麻辣 málà — numbing-and-hot / verdovend-pittig — the default Sichuan/Chongqing profile. 酸 suān — sour / zuur. 甜 tián — sweet / zoet. 咸 xián — salty / zout. 香 xiāng — fragrant, savoury-good / geurig, lekker. 鲜 xiān — umami, fresh / hartig, umami. 苦 kǔ — bitter / bitter. 臭 chòu — stinky, and proudly so / stinkend — 臭豆腐. 怪味 guàiwèi — 'strange flavour', an actual Sichuan flavour category / een echt smaakprofiel. 五香 wǔxiāng — five-spice / vijfkruiden. 孜然 zīrán — cumin / komijn. 芥末 jièmo — mustard, wasabi / mosterd, wasabi. 花椒 huājiāo — Sichuan pepper / Sichuanpeper. 辣椒 làjiāo — chilli / chilipeper. 剁椒 duòjiāo — chopped pickled chilli / gehakte ingelegde chili. 泡椒 pàojiāo — pickled chilli / ingelegde chili. 小米辣 xiǎomǐlà — bird's-eye chilli, very hot / rawitpeper, zeer heet. 蒜蓉 suànróng — minced garlic / fijngehakte knoflook. 葱 cōng — spring onion / lente-ui. 姜 jiāng — ginger / gember. 香菜 xiāngcài — coriander / koriander — worth learning purely so you can say 不要香菜.
Heat dialling: 不辣 bù là — not spicy / niet pittig. 免辣 miǎn là — hold the chilli / zonder chili. 微辣 wēi là — mildly spicy / licht pittig. 中辣 zhōng là — medium / medium. 重辣 / 特辣 zhòng là / tè là — very hot / zeer heet. 变态辣 biàntài là — 'perverted hot' / 'perverse' heet — a real menu option, not a joke. 加辣 jiā là — extra chilli / extra chili. 少辣 shǎo là — less chilli / minder chili. NOTE: 微辣 in Chengdu is hotter than 特辣 in Shanghai; the scale is local, not national.
Organ and texture set: 肠 cháng — intestine / darm — 肥肠, 大肠. 肚 dǔ — tripe, stomach / pens, maag — 毛肚 ox tripe, 猪肚 pig stomach; the same character read dù means 'belly'. 肝 gān — liver / lever — 猪肝, 鹅肝. 血 xuè / xiě — blood, served as a set curd / bloed, als gestolde koek — 鸭血, 毛血旺. 舌 shé — tongue / tong — 牛舌, also written 口条. 筋 jīn — tendon / pees — 牛筋, 蹄筋. 心 xīn — heart / hart — 鸡心, 猪心 (心 also means 'centre' and 'filling', so 菜心 is a vegetable). 腰 yāo — kidney / nier — 腰花, 猪腰; 腰 also means 'waist'. 脑 nǎo — brain / hersenen — 脑花. 皮 pí — skin / huid, zwoerd — 猪皮, 鸡皮, 皮蛋 century egg.
Extended: 肺 fèi — lung / long. 肾 shèn — kidney / nier. 蹄 tí — trotter / poot. 爪 zhǎo (in compounds) / zhuǎ (colloquial, 爪子) — feet, claws / pootjes — 凤爪 fèngzhǎo, 鸡爪 jīzhǎo chicken feet. 胗 zhēn — gizzard / spiermaag. 翅 chì — wing / vleugel. 掌 zhǎng — webbed foot / zwemvlies-poot. 骨 gǔ — bone / bot. 尾 wěi — tail / staart. 头 tóu — head / kop. 黄喉 huánghóu — aorta / aorta, a hotpot delicacy.
Teach the flesh radical ⺼ (U+2EBC) as one card BEFORE 肠 肚 肝 肺 肾 腰 脑 胗. Exceptions: 血, 皮 and 舌 do NOT carry it; 筋 carries it inside 肋 but takes ⺮ as its Kangxi radical. For 麻, do not gloss it as a word — give it a dedicated card and the sentence 'this is not heat, it is your mouth going numb; there is no Dutch word for it'. Ship 不要香菜 / 不辣 / 微辣 as a separate always-accessible 'point at this' screen at large type.
directives.basis: Component membership verified independently this session against makemeahanzi: all eight organ characters carry ⺼ U+2EBC, and 期/朋 carry 月 U+6708 — the codepoint correction is load-bearing. 凤爪/鸡爪 readings and 'minced' corrected. Every organ term and 麻 麻辣 酸 咸 鲜 are measured absent from HSK 3.0's first 900.

directives.directive:
MENU STRAND 4 — qualifiers and section headers. 时价 is the most expensive two characters a traveller can fail to read.
Portion and price: 大份 dà fèn — large portion / grote portie. 中份 zhōng fèn — medium / medium. 小份 xiǎo fèn — small / kleine portie. 半份 bàn fèn — half portion / halve portie. 例 lì — standard portion, common on chain and southern menus / standaardportie. 位 wèi — per person / per persoon. 时价 shí jià — MARKET PRICE: no price is printed and you will be told after you eat / dagprijs. 起 qǐ — 'from' / vanaf — 88元起. 招牌 zhāopái — signature dish / huisspecialiteit. 特色 tèsè — house specialty / specialiteit. 推荐 / 店长推荐 tuījiàn — recommended / aanbevolen. 新品 xīnpǐn — new / nieuw. 热销 rèxiāo — best-seller / bestseller. 现做 xiànzuò — made to order / vers bereid. 限量 xiànliàng — limited quantity / beperkt beschikbaar. 套餐 tàocān — set meal / menu, combinatie. 单点 dāndiǎn — à la carte / los bestellen. 配 pèi — served with / geserveerd met. 另收费 lìng shōufèi — charged separately / apart in rekening gebracht. 茶位费 chá wèi fèi — tea/cover charge per head, standard in Guangdong / couvert per persoon. 餐位费 cān wèi fèi — cover charge / couvert. 餐盒费 / 打包费 cān hé fèi — takeaway box fee / verpakkingskosten. 服务费 fúwù fèi — service charge / bedieningsgeld.
Dietary: 素 sù — vegetarian / vegetarisch — but 素 dishes routinely contain 蚝油 or 高汤. 全素 quán sù — strictly vegetarian / strikt vegetarisch. 斋 zhāi — Buddhist vegetarian, the reliable one / boeddhistisch vegetarisch, de betrouwbare. 荤 hūn — meat-containing / met vlees. 清真 qīngzhēn — halal / halal. 忌口 jìkǒu — dietary restriction / dieetbeperking.
Section headers in menu order: 凉菜 liángcài — cold dishes / koude gerechten. 热菜 rècài — hot dishes / warme gerechten. 荤菜 hūncài — meat dishes / vleesgerechten. 素菜 sùcài — vegetable dishes / groentegerechten. 海鲜 hǎixiān — seafood / zeevruchten. 烧烤 shāokǎo — grilled, skewers / gegrild, spiesjes. 主食 zhǔshí — staples: rice, noodles, buns; ordered LAST in China, not first / basisgerechten, worden als laatste besteld. 汤 / 汤类 / 汤羹 tāng — soups / soepen. 小吃 xiǎochī — snacks, small plates / kleine gerechten. 甜品 / 甜点 tiánpǐn — dessert / nagerecht. 饮料 yǐnliào — soft drinks / frisdrank. 酒水 jiǔshuǐ — alcohol and drinks / alcohol en dranken. 时令 shílìng — seasonal / seizoensgebonden.
directives.basis: Pinyin mechanically verified. 招牌 特色 时价 大份 例 凉菜 热菜 主食 all measured absent from HSK 2.0 L1-3. The 主食-comes-last convention is a cultural fact worth an explicit card for Dutch diners.

directives.directive:
QR / MINI-PROGRAMME TRANSACTION VOCABULARY — a sixth card template rendering a phone-inside-a-phone: a scrollable Chinese ordering UI at realistic 14-16px density with tappable buttons. The task is not 'what does this character mean' but 'tap the button that adds this to your cart without ordering it'.
In the order you meet it: 扫码点餐 sǎomǎ diǎncān — scan to order / scan om te bestellen. 扫一扫 sǎo yī sǎo — scan / scannen. 请扫码点单 — please scan to order. 堂食 tángshí — dine in / ter plaatse eten. 外卖 wàimài — delivery / bezorging. 打包 dǎbāo — takeaway / meenemen. 桌号 zhuōhào — table number / tafelnummer. 人数 rénshù — number of diners / aantal personen. 点餐 diǎncān — order / bestellen. 规格 guīgé — specification, size / maat, variant. 口味 kǒuwèi — taste option, where 微辣/中辣 lives / smaakoptie. 数量 shùliàng — quantity / aantal. 加入购物车 jiārù gòuwùchē — add to cart / in winkelwagen. 购物车 gòuwùchē — cart / winkelwagen. 备注 bèizhù — notes to kitchen / opmerkingen — the field where 不要香菜 goes. 去结算 qù jiésuàn — go to checkout / naar afrekenen. 提交订单 tíjiāo dìngdān — submit order / bestelling plaatsen. 下单 xiàdān — place order / bestellen. 起送 qǐsòng — minimum order / minimum bestelbedrag. 优惠券 yōuhuìquàn — voucher / kortingsbon. 满减 mǎnjiǎn — spend-X-get-Y-off / bij besteding X, Y korting. 支付 zhīfù — pay / betalen. 微信支付 / 支付宝 — WeChat Pay / Alipay. 扫码支付 sǎomǎ zhīfù — scan to pay. 现金 xiànjīn — cash / contant. 不收现金 — no cash accepted. 确认 quèrèn — confirm / bevestigen. 取消 qǔxiāo — cancel / annuleren. 已售 yǐshòu — number sold / aantal verkocht. 售罄 shòuqìng — sold out / uitverkocht. 呼叫服务员 hūjiào fúwùyuán — call the waiter / ober roepen. 买单 / 结账 mǎidān / jiézhàng — the bill / afrekenen. 开发票 kāi fāpiào — issue an official invoice / factuur (fapiao) aanvragen.
The two pairs that matter most and are easiest to confuse: 去结算 (checkout, proceed) vs 取消 (cancel); 提交订单 (submit, irreversible) vs 加入购物车 (add to cart, reversible). Author ~25 items. This is the only template where small type is correct, because small type IS the difficulty. Add a timed 'ordering flow' at the top bet tier: five taps in 40 seconds.
directives.basis: Practitioner-derived; the QR-menu shift is a market-research claim needing a field study, not a literature claim. But it PROMOTES: this is one of only three situations where reading genuinely beats camera OCR (a mini-programme cannot be photographed by a second phone), and 去结算 提交订单 售罄 are all measured absent from every HSK level. Requires interaction: 'choice' | 'tap-target' plus a hit-region spec in the item schema — add it now rather than retrofitting.

directives.directive:
TRANSIT STRAND 1 — metro. Core set: 地铁 dìtiě — metro / metro. 站 zhàn — station, stop / station, halte. 号线 hào xiàn — line number / lijnnummer — 4号线 = Line 4. 出口 chūkǒu — exit / uitgang. 入口 rùkǒu — entrance / ingang. 出入口 chūrùkǒu — entrance/exit / in- en uitgang. 换乘 huànchéng — transfer, change lines / overstappen. 方向 fāngxiàng — direction / richting. 开往 kāi wǎng — bound for / richting, naar — followed by the TERMINUS name, which is the actual information. 首班车 shǒubānchē — first train / eerste trein. 末班车 mòbānchē — last train / laatste trein. 首末班车时间 — first/last train times. 单程票 dānchéngpiào — single journey ticket / enkeltje. 进站 jìnzhàn — enter the station / station in. 出站 chūzhàn — exit the station / station uit. 安检 ānjiǎn — security check, MANDATORY on every Chinese metro, bags on the belt / veiligheidscontrole, verplicht. 站台 zhàntái — platform / perron. 站厅 zhàntīng — concourse / stationshal. 付费区 fùfèiqū — paid area / betaalde zone. 非付费区 fēifùfèiqū — unpaid area / onbetaalde zone — the trap: crossing between them costs a fare. 自动售票机 zìdòng shòupiàojī — ticket machine / kaartautomaat. 售票处 shòupiàochù — ticket office / loket. 服务中心 fúwù zhōngxīn — service centre / servicebalie. 补票 bǔpiào — fare adjustment / bijbetalen. 无障碍 wúzhàng'ài — accessible, step-free / rolstoeltoegankelijk. 电梯 diàntī — lift / lift. 扶梯 fútī — escalator / roltrap. 失物招领 shīwù zhāolǐng — lost property / gevonden voorwerpen.
Compass, used in exit names, station names and street names: 东 dōng — east / oost. 西 xī — west / west. 南 nán — south / zuid. 北 běi — north / noord. 中 zhōng — central / centrum. Street types: 路 lù — road / weg. 街 jiē — street / straat. 道 dào — avenue / laan. 大街 dàjiē — main street / hoofdstraat. 大道 dàdào — boulevard / boulevard. 巷 / 弄 / 胡同 — alley / steeg. 环 huán — ring road / ringweg — 内环 inner, 外环 outer.
EXIT LETTERING, which differs by city and is documented nowhere a traveller looks: Beijing uses LETTERS with a compass gloss ('A 西北口' = exit A, northwest). Guangzhou and Shenzhen use letters with numeric subdivisions (A, B1, B2, C). Shanghai and Nanjing use NUMBERS (1号口, 2号口). Hong Kong MTR uses letter+number (A1, B2). Chengdu and Xi'an use letters. In all systems the exit letter is the addressable unit — 'meet me at C口', where 口 means 'exit', not 'mouth'. Floors: 层 céng — floor / verdieping; B1, B2 are basement levels; 3楼 sān lóu counts the ground floor as 1, so 3楼 is de tweede verdieping in Dutch, not de derde. Ship this off-by-one as an explicit Dutch-gloss warning card — it is a Dutch-and-European-specific error the English gloss does not surface.
directives.basis: Practitioner-derived. Weight this domain at only ~5% of the bag: tier-1 metros, HSR and airports are heavily bilingual in observed practice. 换乘 安全出口 无障碍 扶梯 失物招领 单程票 are measured absent from every HSK level. The 3楼 off-by-one is an unsourced observation, not a finding.

directives.directive:
TRANSIT STRAND 2 — rail and airport. Rail: 火车 huǒchē — train / trein. 火车站 huǒchēzhàn — railway station / treinstation. 高铁 gāotiě — high-speed rail, G-trains / hogesnelheidstrein. 动车 dòngchē — D-trains, slightly slower / sneltrein. 候车 hòuchē — wait for the train / wachten op de trein. 候车室 hòuchēshì — waiting hall / wachtruimte. 检票 jiǎnpiào — ticket check / kaartcontrole. 检票口 jiǎnpiàokǒu — ticket gate / controlepoort. 站台 zhàntái — platform / perron. 车厢 chēxiāng — carriage, coach / rijtuig, wagon. 座位号 zuòwèihào — seat number / stoelnummer. 检票时间 — boarding time / instaptijd — HSR gates CLOSE a few minutes before departure and do not reopen; the single most common way a visitor misses a Chinese train.
Seat-class grid, taught as ONE 2×2 card (4 characters, 8 signs): 硬 yìng — hard / hard. 软 ruǎn — soft / zacht. 座 zuò — seat / zitplaats. 卧 wò — berth, sleeper / slaapplaats. → 硬座 yìngzuò — hard seat, cheapest, upright / harde zit. 软座 ruǎnzuò — soft seat / zachte zit. 硬卧 yìngwò — hard sleeper, open six-berth bay, three tiers / harde slaapplaats, open coupé met zes bedden. 软卧 ruǎnwò — soft sleeper, four-berth closed compartment / zachte slaapplaats, gesloten coupé met vier bedden. High-speed ladder: 二等座 èrděngzuò — second class / tweede klas. 一等座 yīděngzuò — first class / eerste klas. 商务座 shāngwùzuò — business class / businessklasse. 无座 wúzuò — standing ticket / staanplaats — on CONVENTIONAL trains priced as 硬座, but on G/D HIGH-SPEED services priced as 二等座, i.e. you pay the full second-class fare and get no seat. Split the gloss by train class.
Ticketing: 身份证 shēnfènzhèng — ID card; foreigners use their PASSPORT 护照, which is why the automatic gates often reject you / identiteitsbewijs. 护照 hùzhào — passport / paspoort. 取票 qǔpiào — collect a printed ticket / ticket ophalen. 人工窗口 réngōng chuāngkǒu — staffed counter, where passport-holders go / bemand loket. 售票厅 shòupiàotīng — ticket hall / ticketbalie. 退票 tuìpiào — refund / ticket annuleren. 改签 gǎiqiān — change ticket / omboeken. 实名制 shímíngzhì — real-name registration / registratie op naam.
Airport: 机场 jīchǎng — airport / luchthaven. 航站楼 hángzhànlóu — terminal / terminal. 出发 chūfā — departures / vertrek. 到达 dàodá — arrivals / aankomst. 国内 guónèi — domestic / binnenland. 国际 guójì — international / internationaal. 值机 zhíjī — check-in / inchecken. 登机口 dēngjīkǒu — boarding gate / gate. 登机牌 dēngjīpái — boarding pass / instapkaart. 托运 tuōyùn — check baggage / bagage inchecken. 行李 xíngli — luggage / bagage. 行李提取 xíngli tíqǔ — baggage claim / bagageband. 安检 ānjiǎn — security / veiligheidscontrole. 边检 biānjiǎn — immigration / paspoortcontrole. 海关 hǎiguān — customs / douane. 中转 zhōngzhuǎn — transfer / overstap. 晚点 wǎndiǎn — delayed / vertraagd. 取消 qǔxiāo — cancelled / geannuleerd. 登机中 dēngjī zhōng — boarding / aan het boarden.
Also teach 出发/到达 × 国内/国际 and 进站/出站 as 2×2 grids. Build a grid2x2 card type with the axis labels as the taught units and all four cells as the tested units — the highest ratio of items-unlocked to characters-learned in the curriculum.
directives.basis: Practitioner-derived; the 无座 pricing correction is flagged for verification against China Railway 12306 fare rules before content lock (all .cn hosts were unreachable). 二等座 单程票 托运 改签 are measured absent from every HSK level.

directives.directive:
SUPERMARKET — the three traps, all measured absent from HSK 2.0 L1-3, all worth more to a traveller than the HSK 1 word list.
斤: 斤 jīn — catty = 500 g exactly / catty = 500 gram. Loose produce, meat and fish are priced 元/斤 almost everywhere, so 12.8元/斤 is 25.6 元/kg — DOUBLE what a European brain computes. 半斤 bàn jīn — 250 g. 两 liǎng — 50 g, one tenth of a 斤 — used for noodles, tea, dumpling weights. 公斤 gōngjīn / 千克 qiānkè — kilogram = 2 斤. 克 kè — gram / gram. 毫升 háoshēng — millilitre. 升 shēng — litre.
折: 折 zhé — discount, expressed as the FRACTION YOU PAY, not the fraction off / korting, uitgedrukt als wat je betaalt. 打八折 dǎ bā zhé — pay 80%, i.e. 20% off. 打五折 — half price. 打七五折 — pay 75%. A European reading '8折' as '80% off' is badly wrong in the wrong direction. 满减 mǎnjiǎn — threshold discount — 满100减20. 第二件半价 dì èr jiàn bàn jià — second item half price. 买一送一 mǎi yī sòng yī — buy one get one free / 1+1 gratis. 特价 tèjià — special price / aanbieding. 促销 cùxiāo — promotion / actie. 原价 yuánjià — original price / oude prijs. 现价 xiànjià — current price / nu. 会员价 huìyuánjià — members' price, requires a scanned app account and the shelf shows it as if it were the price / ledenprijs. 清仓 qīngcāng — clearance / opruiming.
保质期: Chinese labels do NOT print an expiry date. They print 生产日期 shēngchǎn rìqī — production date / productiedatum — plus 保质期 bǎozhìqī — shelf life as a DURATION / houdbaarheidsduur — e.g. 保质期12个月. You must add them. Also 见包装 jiàn bāozhuāng — 'see the packaging'; 见瓶身 jiàn píngshēn — 'see the bottle'; 见喷码 jiàn pēnmǎ — 'see the inkjet code'. 保质期至 bǎozhìqī zhì — best before (a real date) / ten minste houdbaar tot. Date formats: 20260822, 2026/08/22, 2026.08.22, 26 08 22.
Storage and the rest: 冷藏 lěngcáng — refrigerate, 0-4°C / gekoeld bewaren. 冷冻 lěngdòng — freeze, -18°C / diepvries. 常温 chángwēn — ambient / kamertemperatuur. 阴凉干燥处 yīnliáng gānzào chù — cool dry place / koel en droog bewaren. 净含量 jìnghánliàng — net content / netto-inhoud. 规格 guīgé — size, spec / verpakkingsmaat. 进口 jìnkǒu — imported / geïmporteerd. 原产国 yuánchǎnguó — country of origin / land van herkomst. 散装 sǎnzhuāng — loose, sold by weight / los, per gewicht. 称重 chēngzhòng — weigh here / hier afwegen — in many Chinese supermarkets you must weigh and get a barcode sticker in the produce section BEFORE checkout. 超市 chāoshì — supermarket / supermarkt. 便利店 biànlìdiàn — convenience store / buurtwinkel. 收银台 shōuyíntái — checkout / kassa. 结账 jiézhàng — pay / afrekenen. 扫码支付 sǎomǎ zhīfù — scan to pay / betalen met QR-code. 元 yuán — yuan, written / yuan. 块 kuài — yuan, spoken / yuan (spreektaal). 角 jiǎo / 毛 máo — 0.1 yuan / 10 cent. 分 fēn — 0.01 yuan / cent.
Build a price-label template where the numeral is huge and the unit character small — that is the real reading condition, and the whole difficulty is that 斤 is 8px next to a 40px number. Task type is itemType:'compute' with a generator so numbers randomise: '牛肉 32.8元/斤 — what does a kilo cost?' (32.8 / 65.6 / 16.4 / 328); '原价 200元, 打七折 — what do you pay?'; production date + 保质期6个月 — is it still good today? Un-skippable, first three market-strand items.
directives.basis: HSK absence MEASURED: 斤 克 千克 净含量 生产日期 保质期 冷藏 冷冻 特价 买一送一 会员价 折 满减 are all outside HSK 2.0 L1-3, and 折 is HSK 2.0 L6. 斤 is at SUBTLEX frequency rank 2,551 — a pure frequency-ordered bank would never reach it. Weight market/label at ~30% of the bag: this is the domain with no English at all (GB 7718 mandates Chinese and caps foreign type size).

directives.directive:
ALLERGEN AND NUTRITION PACK — optional, unlocked by the dietary-flags onboarding, using a real ingredient-list template (10pt grey paragraph text, the actual reading condition) with a scan-and-find task ('is there soy in this?') on a 15-second timer, not a recognition task.
配料表 pèiliàobiǎo — ingredients list / ingrediëntenlijst. 配料 pèiliào — ingredients / ingrediënten. 含 hán — contains / bevat. 不含 bù hán — does not contain / bevat geen. 可能含有 kěnéng hányǒu — may contain / kan sporen bevatten. 过敏原 guòmǐnyuán — allergen / allergeen. 麸质 fūzhì — gluten / gluten. 小麦 xiǎomài — wheat / tarwe. 大豆 dàdòu — soy / soja. 花生 huāshēng — peanut / pinda. 坚果 jiānguǒ — tree nuts / noten. 乳 rǔ — milk / melk. 牛奶 niúnǎi — cow's milk / koemelk. 乳糖 rǔtáng — lactose / lactose. 蛋 dàn — egg / ei. 鱼 yú — fish / vis. 虾 xiā — shrimp / garnaal. 甲壳类 jiǎqiàolèi — crustaceans / schaaldieren. 芝麻 zhīma — sesame / sesam. 食品添加剂 shípǐn tiānjiājì — food additives / additieven. 营养成分表 yíngyǎng chéngfèn biǎo — nutrition table / voedingswaardetabel. 能量 néngliàng — energy, in kJ / energie, in kJ. 蛋白质 dànbáizhì — protein / eiwit. 脂肪 zhīfáng — fat / vet. 碳水化合物 tànshuǐ huàhéwù — carbohydrate / koolhydraten. 钠 nà — sodium / natrium. 糖 táng — sugar / suiker. 味精 wèijīng — MSG / ve-tsin. 鸡精 jījīng — chicken bouillon powder, contains chicken / kippenbouillonpoeder, bevat kip. 猪油 zhūyóu — lard / reuzel. 明胶 míngjiāo — gelatine / gelatine. 清真 qīngzhēn — halal / halal.
The eight GB 7718-2011 allergen categories, declaration RECOMMENDED not mandatory: 含麸质的谷物, 甲壳纲类动物, 鱼类, 蛋类, 花生, 大豆, 乳 (incl. 乳糖), 坚果. GUARDRAIL: state plainly, once, that the app is a game and not a medical tool and that absence of a warning on a Chinese label does not mean absence of the allergen.
directives.basis: GB 7718-2011 and GB 28050 cited but the standard texts were unreachable. A 2025 revision believed to move allergen labelling toward mandatory (transition into 2027) must be verified before any claim about it ships. 能量 is declared in kJ not kcal — a factor of ~4.184 that silently misleads European readers.

directives.directive:
SHOPFRONTS — order the strand HEADS FIRST. Chinese business names are head-final compounds, so the LAST character carries the category. Eight head morphemes before any complete business name: 店 diàn — shop / winkel (药店, 书店, 花店, 便利店, 水果店, 眼镜店). 铺 pù — shop, older/smaller / winkeltje (店铺, 杂货铺). 馆 guǎn — an establishment, a house of / gelegenheid (面馆, 饭馆, 茶馆, 宾馆, 图书馆, 博物馆). 厅 tīng — hall / zaal (餐厅, 咖啡厅, 大厅). 行 háng (NOT xíng) — a trade house / handelshuis (银行, 车行, 商行). 城 chéng — used for large retail / markthal, centrum (美食城, 家具城, 电脑城). 场 chǎng — a venue / terrein, plein (停车场, 广场, 市场, 商场). 中心 zhōngxīn — centre / centrum (购物中心, 服务中心). Plus 屋, 坊, 阁, 轩, 家, 记 (老王记, 'Old Wang's') as boutique/traditional heads.
Business names to identify from the sign alone: 药店 / 药房 yàodiàn / yàofáng — pharmacy, GREEN CROSS / apotheek. 医院 yīyuàn — hospital / ziekenhuis. 诊所 zhěnsuǒ — clinic / huisartsenpraktijk. 社区卫生服务中心 — community health centre. 急诊 jízhěn — A&E / spoedeisende hulp. 银行 yínháng — bank / bank (中国银行 the one that reliably changes foreign currency, 工商银行, 建设银行, 农业银行, 招商银行). 自动取款机 / ATM — cash machine / geldautomaat. 邮局 yóujú / 中国邮政 — post office, GREEN livery / postkantoor. 派出所 pàichūsuǒ — local police station / politiebureau. 公安局 gōng'ānjú — public security bureau. 出入境管理 chūrùjìng guǎnlǐ — exit-entry administration, where visa extensions happen / vreemdelingendienst. 厕所 cèsuǒ — toilet, blunt / wc. 洗手间 xǐshǒujiān — washroom, polite / toilet. 卫生间 wèishēngjiān — bathroom / toilet. 公厕 gōngcè — public toilet / openbaar toilet. 酒店 jiǔdiàn — hotel, larger / hotel. 宾馆 bīnguǎn — hotel, mid-range / hotel. 招待所 zhāodàisuǒ — guesthouse, basic, often no foreigners / eenvoudig pension. 民宿 mínsù — homestay / bed and breakfast. 客栈 kèzhàn — inn / herberg. 饭店 fàndiàn — CONFUSING: means both restaurant and hotel / betekent zowel restaurant als hotel. 餐厅 cāntīng — restaurant. 餐馆 cānguǎn — restaurant. 食堂 shítáng — canteen / kantine. 小吃 xiǎochī — snacks, cheap eats / snackbar. 面馆 miànguǎn — noodle shop / noedelzaak. 米粉 mǐfěn — rice-noodle shop / rijstnoedelzaak. 火锅 huǒguō — hotpot / hotpot. 烧烤 shāokǎo — BBQ skewers, evening / barbecue. 串串 chuànchuàn — skewer hotpot. 自助餐 zìzhùcān — buffet / buffet. 咖啡 kāfēi / 咖啡厅 — coffee / koffie. 茶 chá / 茶楼 chálóu — tea / thee, theehuis. 奶茶 nǎichá — bubble tea / bubbelthee. 理发 lǐfà / 美发 měifà — barber, hairdresser / kapper. 美容 měiróng — beauty salon / schoonheidssalon. 洗衣 xǐyī / 干洗 gānxǐ — laundry, dry cleaning / wasserij, stomerij. 快递 kuàidì — courier, parcel point / pakketpunt (顺丰 SF, 中通, 圆通, 菜鸟驿站 Cainiao). 加油站 jiāyóuzhàn — petrol station / tankstation (中石化 Sinopec, 中石油 PetroChina). 停车场 tíngchēchǎng — car park / parkeerplaats (signed P, 地下车库 underground). 超市 chāoshì / 便利店 biànlìdiàn — supermarket, convenience store (全家 FamilyMart, 罗森 Lawson, 美宜佳). 商场 shāngchǎng / 购物中心 / 百货 / 广场 — mall, department store, plaza / winkelcentrum, warenhuis. 市场 shìchǎng / 菜市场 càishìchǎng — market, wet market / markt, versmarkt. 手机维修 shǒujī wéixiū — phone repair / telefoonreparatie. 按摩 ànmó / 足疗 zúliáo — massage, foot massage. 网吧 wǎngbā — internet café / internetcafé. 健身房 jiànshēnfáng — gym / sportschool. 眼镜店 yǎnjìngdiàn — optician / opticien. 水果店 shuǐguǒdiàn — fruit shop / fruitwinkel. 图书馆 túshūguǎn — library / bibliotheek.
Second-tier task is GENERATIVE: show a shopfront the player has never seen (电脑城, 花店, 修车行) and ask what KIND of place it is, answerable from the head alone. Log unseenCompoundAccuracy as a separate metric — it measures generalisation rather than recall.
directives.basis: Rests on a well-supported structural fact: Chinese nominal compounds are overwhelmingly head-final. 行 háng in 银行 and 美发 měifà verified correct by pypinyin — exactly the heteronyms sloppy sources get wrong. This is the only strand where a player can correctly answer an item not in the bank. Apply the traditional-variant rendering here specifically (理发/理髮, 面馆/麵館): fascias favour calligraphic lettering, which is legally permitted to be traditional.

directives.directive:
UNIVERSAL SIGNAGE — openers, formulas, opposite pairs, numbers, money, dates.
Openers in decreasing force: 严禁 yánjìn — strictly forbidden / streng verboden. 禁止 jìnzhǐ — prohibited / verboden. 不准 bù zhǔn — not permitted / niet toegestaan. 请勿 qǐng wù — please do not, polite / gelieve niet. 谢绝 xièjué — politely declined / niet toegestaan. 注意 zhùyì — attention / let op. 小心 xiǎoxīn — be careful / voorzichtig, pas op. 当心 dāngxīn — beware / pas op. 危险 wēixiǎn — danger / gevaar.
Full signs: 禁止吸烟 jìnzhǐ xīyān — no smoking / verboden te roken. 禁止通行 jìnzhǐ tōngxíng — no entry, no through traffic / verboden doorgang. 禁止停车 — no parking. 禁止拍照 — no photography. 请勿触摸 — do not touch / niet aanraken. 请勿入内 / 闲人免进 — no entry, staff only / verboden toegang. 小心地滑 xiǎoxīn dì huá — caution wet floor / pas op, gladde vloer. 当心碰头 — mind your head / pas op uw hoofd. 小心台阶 — mind the step / pas op de trede. 安全出口 ānquán chūkǒu — emergency exit, GREEN / nooduitgang, groen. 消防通道 xiāofáng tōngdào — fire lane, keep clear / brandgang. 灭火器 mièhuǒqì — fire extinguisher / brandblusser. 施工中 shīgōng zhōng — under construction / werk in uitvoering. 正在维修 / 故障 gùzhàng — out of order / buiten gebruik. 暂停使用 zàntíng shǐyòng — temporarily out of use / tijdelijk buiten gebruik. 请排队 qǐng páiduì — please queue / graag in de rij.
Opposite pairs, authored as ONE card with two halves, never two cards: 入 rù / 出 chū — in / uit. 开 kāi / 关 guān — open, on / dicht, uit. 推 tuī / 拉 lā — push / trekken. 上 shàng / 下 xià — up, board / down, alight. 左 zuǒ / 右 yòu — links / rechts. 前 qián / 后 hòu — voor / achter. 内 nèi / 外 wài — binnen / buiten. 免费 miǎnfèi / 收费 shōufèi — gratis / betaald. 营业中 yíngyè zhōng / 休息 xiūxi — geopend / gesloten, pauze. 停业 tíngyè — closed down / gesloten (permanent). 满 mǎn / 空 kōng — vol / vrij, leeg — on car parks and toilet cubicles. 有人 yǒu rén / 无人 wú rén — bezet / vrij. 男 nán / 女 nǚ — heren / dames — learn as a pair and never in isolation.
NUMBERS: 一二三四五六七八九十 yī èr sān sì wǔ liù qī bā jiǔ shí, 百 bǎi, 千 qiān, 万 wàn TEN THOUSAND — the 万 unit is a genuine obstacle because Chinese counts in units of 10,000, so 十万 = 100,000 and 一百万 = 1,000,000; 亿 yì = 100,000,000. 零 / 〇 líng. 两 liǎng = 'two of something', used instead of 二 before measure words.
FINANCIAL CAPITAL FORMS 大写, on bank forms, receipts, contracts, invoices and banknotes: 壹 yī 1, 贰 èr 2, 叁 sān 3, 肆 sì 4, 伍 wǔ 5, 陆 liù 6, 柒 qī 7, 捌 bā 8, 玖 jiǔ 9, 拾 shí 10, 佰 bǎi 100, 仟 qiān 1000, 萬 wàn 10000, 圆/元 yuán, 角 jiǎo, 分 fēn. A 100-yuan note reads 壹佰圆. Practical priority: 壹 贰 叁 拾 佰 圆.
MONEY: 元 written / 块 spoken; 角 written / 毛 spoken = 0.1; 分 = 0.01, effectively extinct. ¥ / RMB / CNY / 人民币.
DATES AND TIMES: 年 nián, 月 yuè, 日 rì (written) / 号 hào (spoken) — 2026年8月22日. 星期一 xīngqīyī / 周一 zhōuyī — maandag; days numbered 一 to 六 then 星期日/星期天. 上午 shàngwǔ, 中午 zhōngwǔ, 下午 xiàwǔ, 晚上 wǎnshang. 点 diǎn, 分 fēn, 半 bàn. 营业时间 yíngyè shíjiān — openingstijden, usually 24-hour (09:00-22:00). 至 zhì / 到 dào — tot. 周一至周五 — maandag t/m vrijdag. 节假日 jiéjiàrì — feestdagen. 全天 quán tiān / 24小时 — de hele dag.
For 万, build a compute item: show 三万五千, ask for the Arabic numeral, distractors at 10× and 0.1×, because the failure mode is an order-of-magnitude error and it costs money. Put 壹贰叁拾佰圆 in a low-priority 'bank counter' sub-deck — high consequence, low encounter rate, available but never blocking.
directives.basis: Pair-learning halves the item count and matches the real discrimination task, which is always binary (which door, which toilet, is it open). Paired simultaneous presentation is the one Chinese-specific finding with direct experimental support (Li, Shi & Wang 2025, N=183). Import the numeral/date/time subset wholesale from HSK — the one place HSK and signage genuinely coincide, ~35 items of pure overlap. 壹贰叁肆伍陆柒捌玖拾佰仟 measured OUTSIDE the official 3,000-character standard, which confirms the low-priority assignment.

directives.directive: RADICAL ONBOARDING — corrected list. Priority one for this domain: 火/灬 (cooking method: 炒 炸 烤 煮 蒸 焖 炖 烧 煎 — 9 of the 13 core methods take it as radical, verified), ⺼ U+2EBC (flesh/body-part: 肠 肚 肝 肺 肾 腰 脑 胗 — NOT 月 U+6708), 饣 (food: 43 characters incl. 饭 饿 馆 饺 饼 饮 — NOT 食, which has 12, mostly traditional). Then 辶 (motion/transit), 门 (gate), 车 (vehicle), 钅 (metal), 氵 (liquid), 忄 (heart), 疒 (illness), 讠 (speech), 纟, 亻, 宀, 刂 (cut: 切 剁 割), 阝 (place: 部 都 邮), 酉 (alcohol/fermented), 米 (grain), 艹 (plant), 鱼, 女, 口. DROP 男 (not a radical — it is 田+力) and 页 (head; its derivative set 顶 顺 须 顾 颈 项 领 颜 额 题 has near-zero menu or signage payoff). Tag 月 items explicitly as meat-radical vs non-meat-radical, or exclude 月 from the taught set entirely — 期 朗 服 有 望 carry the moon component or a graphic merger and will misfire.
directives.basis: Radical counts and cooking-method radicals verified independently this session against makemeahanzi (饣 43, 食 12, 火 128, 灬 28, 刂 71, 阝 160). Explicit semantic-radical instruction transfers to inferring meanings of UNTAUGHT characters containing taught radicals (Frontiers 2017, PMC5660119; Chen et al. 2013 LLT, N=129). Batch new items into radical-based sets of 6-8 for beginners rather than interleaving across radicals.

directives.directive: TIER STRUCTURE AND DOMAIN WEIGHTS. Tier 0 = ~24 items (above), linear and unskippable. Tier 1 = ~110 items: cooking methods (13), proteins (10), staples (8), section headers (8), the 折 and 保质期 traps with their arithmetic, 冷藏/冷冻, 特价/会员价/买一送一, 净含量/克/千克, the eight shopfront head morphemes, 药店 医院 银行 邮局 派出所 加油站 停车场 快递 超市 便利店, the opposite pairs 开/关 上/下 内/外 前/后 左/右, numerals to 万, dates/times/营业时间, and the mini-programme button set (下单 购物车 去结算 备注 确认 取消). Tier 2 = ~200 items: organ and texture set, extended flavour, menu qualifiers and 时价, full transit (metro + rail seat-class grid + airport), allergen and nutrition set, extended shopfronts, 壹贰叁 financial numerals, and composite whole-sign and whole-menu tasks. Category bag weights: market/label 30%, menu 30%, street/shopfront 20%, safety/universal 15%, transit 5%. Total ~380 characters for functional literacy across all five domains.
directives.basis: Ordering is practitioner-derived and the weights have no empirical basis in encounter frequency — nobody has measured how many signs of each type a visitor needs to read per day. Treat as a v1 guess. The mixing (shuffled bag) is the right default and should be defended explicitly: interleaving depresses perceived learning while improving retention and discrimination, so do NOT block by domain to make players feel better. Tier 0 is the correct exception — interleaving benefits assume a familiarity base a cold-start player lacks.

directives.directive: Seed the item bank from CTW rather than from a frequency list or from practitioner judgement alone: compute the character-level signage frequency distribution from its ~1M labelled instances, and use it both to order the bank and to build the held-out sign set. Label every item with provenance: 'corpus' | 'practitioner' | 'capture' and surface it in the about screen. If the photo-capture feature survives at all, ship it strictly on-device: no GPS, no peer sync of images, no server-side pooling — store only the extracted character list, never the photograph or the coordinates.
directives.basis: CTW verified first-party this session. This also removes a legal exposure nobody costed: photographing and geotagging in China touches restrictions on photographing certain installations and on surveying/mapping by foreign nationals, and moving image plus geolocation data off-device engages PIPL for Chinese subjects and GDPR for the Dutch/EU user base. Route to counsel before a line of code if pooled capture survives.

directives.directive: ITEM SCHEMA, decided before any content is authored. Per TOKEN (not per character): pinyin_citation, pinyin_surface, heteronym: bool, sandhi: bool, neutral-tone state per syllable. Per ITEM: gloss {nl, en} both populated from day one; segmentation as an array of word tokens, never a raw string; componentChars[]; isCompositional: bool (出口 yes, 保质期/时价/招牌/方便面 no); atomic: bool for fixed signs; picturable: bool; distractors[] as an authored first-class field with whyPlausible; contexts: Set<TemplateId>; interaction: 'choice' | 'tap-target'; itemType including 'compute'; tradVariants: string[] (never a single nullable value); provenance; templateId. Per CHARACTER: strokeCount, structure enum (left-right / top-bottom / enclosure / atomic), etymology type, phonetic-reliability field computed over the bank itself, freqRank (both general and domain), hsk_version + hsk_band, gf0025_level, vwo_400.
directives.basis: Every field here fixes a measured defect: 39.4% polyphony breaks per-character pinyin; 6.9% one-to-many simplification breaks a nullable traditional column; ~47% of the top 1,000 has no meaning+sound decomposition so a structure enum must drive layout selection; per-bank phonetic reliability is ~17% exact versus ~34% dictionary-wide. Retrofitting a second gloss language into a live bank is the expensive version of that decision.

directives.directive: Make the progress metric 'signs you can act on', never 'characters known' and never a coverage percentage. Store a held-out validation set of ~120 real composite signs (sourced from CTW, which makes it reproducible and publishable) tagged with the character set each requires, and compute signsActionable = |{s : requiredChars(s) ⊆ masteredChars}|. Home screen shows '43 of 120 real signs' with a photo strip. This also self-orders the curriculum: greedily pick the next character that unlocks the most unactionable signs — a set-cover heuristic, which surfaces 期, 质, 净, 含 ahead of higher-frequency but sign-inert characters. Phrase it 'recognised in practice', not 'can read', and calibrate periodically with a harder recall-like format (a 12-option grid, or free typing of the meaning), scaling the displayed number by the measured recognition/recall ratio — a 4-option format has a 25% guess floor and overestimates the cued-recall knowledge an unaided sign requires.
directives.basis: Coverage-to-item arithmetic (0.40^4 ≈ 2.6%) plus the measured genre gap: on a realistic signage/menu character set ~51% of characters fall outside the top 600 and ~64% of menu characters outside the top 1,000, so a corpus-derived coverage meter would tell players they can read 78% of a sign when they cannot read half a menu. This metric is also the right counterweight to interleaving depressing perceived learning: it rises visibly even while within-session accuracy feels erratic.

directives.directive: Wire an actual evaluation from the pieces already designed. Split the ~120-sign held-out set into pre-test and post-test blocks matched on required-character count; administer the pre-test during Tier 0 onboarding (it doubles as the cold-start calibration the multiplayer game needs anyway) and the post-test on landing day via the local notification. Report one number: sign completion rate before departure versus on arrival. Stack the two A/B tests inside it — object-templated versus plain rendering measured on naked-probe accuracy, and the spacing coefficient (0.15 versus ~0.27) measured on landing-day retention. That is the only outcome measure in this product category that is not self-reported.
directives.basis: Three quarters of this study is already specified across the sweeps and nobody connected the pieces. CTW removes the main cost objection to building the held-out set. Instrument the object-template question from v1: templates are the most expensive part of the design and the environmental-print evidence is genuinely contested.

directives.directive: Ship per-city station-name packs as separately downloadable bundles — city/beijing.json with the ~400 station names of that network, city/shanghai.json, etc., 20-40 KB each, cached locally and selected at onboarding ('where are you going?'). Generate transit items procedurally: 开往{terminus}方向 with three sibling termini from the same network as distractors — free content, and exactly the real discrimination task. Without the packs the transit strand teaches 开往 and then shows a station name the player will never see.
directives.basis: Practitioner-derived. The terminus proper noun is the actual information in 开往 X 方向 and it appears in no wordlist.

directives.directive: Enumerate every external host the PWA touches at runtime and confirm each is reachable from inside China, before ship. Three known failures: (1) Google Fonts is blocked — self-host a build-time woff2 subset generated from the bank's own character inventory (measured: 60.0 KB for 482 glyphs versus 7.95 MB for the full face; ~180 KB for sans 400 + sans 700 + serif 400) and precache it in the service worker. (2) WebRTC STUN — the near-universal default stun.l.google.com:19302 is a Google host. For a CO-LOCATED game you need no NAT traversal at all: all phones are on the same LAN or hotspot, so configure an EMPTY iceServers array rather than inheriting a library default, elect a host device, share a join code by QR, and connect on host candidates only. Test with the device in aeroplane mode plus hotspot — the realistic condition in a Chinese restaurant basement. If a relay is ever needed, self-host coturn in-region. (3) iOS Safari evicts script-writable storage (IndexedDB, Cache API, service-worker caches) after roughly seven days of non-use for sites not installed to the home screen — which silently deletes exactly the returning-user history the churn-first architecture exists to protect. Test the seven-day eviction case explicitly in QA and treat local storage as cache, not as the primary store.
directives.basis: Font sizes and the subset were measured this session; the blocking claims are documented but not verifiable from this sandbox and need a mainland vantage point — the engineering fixes are correct regardless. A four-player co-located game whose peers cannot discover each other in the country it was built for is a total product failure, not a degradation.

directives.directive: Do not build or buy neural knowledge tracing, and do not hand-roll SM-2. A four-phone co-located game generates single-digit-thousands of events per user at best — the exact small-data regime where deep knowledge tracing loses to well-featured logistic regression and to plain IRT, and part of DKT's original headline advantage traced to duplicate-record preprocessing artifacts. Use FSRS (MIT-licensed JS/TS ports run offline in a service worker) or a simple Elo/IRT per-item difficulty plus per-player ability estimate. FSRS additionally exposes an explicit retrievability estimate, which is exactly the quantity needed to pick an item that is due for SEVERAL players at once — the scheduling conflict at the heart of a shared round, which a last-write-wins sync design does not address. Sync per (player_id, item_id, attribute) so offline sessions on four phones merge cleanly, and make every card answered in a shared session write back to that player's individual schedule.
directives.basis: Gervet et al. (2020, JEDM); Wilson et al. (2016, EDM); Xiong et al. (2016, EDM); Settles & Meeder (2016, ACL P16-1174) — half-life regression trained on ~12M Duolingo sessions beat Leitner and Pimsleur heuristics and improved engagement in a live A/B. All cited from knowledge, unverified this session.

directives.directive: Set hanzi size from a stored strokeCount, not one global value, and never use a Light or Thin weight — stroke width is the binding constraint on complex glyphs. Treat all specific pixel figures as a starting point for an in-house legibility test on target devices, not as a spec: no study reports them. The genuinely dense SIMPLIFIED survival characters warranting a size bump are 警 19, 藏 17, 燥 17, 糖 16, 醋 15, 辣 14, 蒸 13, 酱 13 — not 檢 續 醬 鹹 餃 質 藥 攤 邊, which are traditional forms that should not appear in the product at all outside the fascia variant rendering. Vary TYPEFACE CLASS per object template (heiti/sans for transit and hazard, songti/serif for printed menus, heavy display for fascias, condensed sans for price labels) rather than chasing photographic fidelity — typeface class is what actually differs in the wild and what a learner must become robust to.
directives.basis: Stroke counts verified this session against makemeahanzi. The legibility literature (Cai/Chi/You 2001; Liu & Yu 2016; Huang/Rau/Liu 2009) is 10-25 years old, desktop/VR, and predates high-DPI phones — direction reliable, magnitude approximate. Environmental context-dependent memory is small and smaller for recognition, so photorealism buys little; CTW's 'wordart' class argues for MORE typeface variation, not fewer templates.

directives.directive: The reveal is a four-row table, not a green tick. Each row: the option's hanzi at ≥32px, its pinyin, its English AND Dutch gloss, and a one-clause note on where you would actually meet it ('冷冻 = vriezer, staat op diepvriesproducten — niet hetzelfde als 冷藏'). The correct row gets the accent bar; wrong rows stay fully legible, never greyed to the point of being skimmed past. Minimum reveal dwell of ~2,000 ms before Next enables. When a player picks a confusable neighbour, show the target and the chosen neighbour side by side with the discriminating component marked. Provide a setting to disable all timers.
directives.basis: Immediate corrective feedback is the established mitigation for multiple-choice lure implantation, and the risk is maximal exactly under a visual-first distractor rule. In a co-located game the reveal is the only moment the non-acting players learn anything. The dwell time and the 40-second timed ordering flow both engage WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable.

directives.directive: Author distractors as a first-class field, never generated randomly, drawn from four confusion families: (a) visually similar characters — 出/山, 天/夭, 未/末, 己/已, 干/千, 人/入, 大/太, 士/土, 日/曰, 微/徽; (b) same-radical semantic neighbours — 肠/肚/肝/肺/肾; (c) real signs from the same object class that mean something dangerously different — 出口 vs 入口, 推 vs 拉, 冷藏 vs 冷冻, 生产日期 vs 保质期, 禁止 vs 请勿, 男 vs 女; (d) same-first-character compounds — 安检/安全/安装, 特价/特色/特产. Family (c) is the highest-value and should be at least 40% of distractors. Exclude the T2↔T3 pinyin swap from the pool for the first 200 items, and exclude polyphones from any 'choose the pinyin' round unless the prompt supplies word context.
directives.basis: Multiple-choice tests with competitive, plausible alternatives produce retention benefits for the tested item and for information related to the incorrect alternatives (Little & Bjork 2015; Little et al. 2012). Visual similarity, not phonology, drives most character errors. But this rule is only safe with mandatory feedback, and pairing pays off only if the distinguishing component is given MEANING — a purely structural breakdown is not enough.

directives.directive: Force transfer out of the object templates. Every character must be met in at least three different object treatments before it graduates: add contexts: Set<TemplateId> to the mastery record and gate graduation on contexts.size >= 3. Add a deliberate 'naked' probe — the character alone, system serif, plain background — at ~10-15% of presentations, and a 'wrong object' probe where 出口 appears in the fascia template instead of the transit plate. Add an Xepsi-style foil: a visually near-identical wrong character in the CORRECT object styling. If a player's naked-probe accuracy trails their in-object accuracy by more than ~20 points, the app is teaching plates rather than characters and should say so.
directives.basis: Masonheimer, Drum & Ehri (1984, n=102): confident environmental-print 'reading' is logo-driven and did not predict decontextualised word reading. This is the cheap insurance against the most expensive part of the design installing a false skill, and it is the instrumentation for the A/B that settles it.

directives.directive: Give the non-acting players a silent parallel task, but make it CUED RECALL, not another four-option tap. While the acting team's timer runs, every other device shows the same sign and a private 'what does this sign make you DO?' with no options shown — answers are not scored, not broadcast, and cost nothing socially, but are recorded to that player's own mastery model. This needs one new local-only event type (shadowAnswer, never gossiped) and no protocol change, since the sign is already replicated to every peer by the existing event log. It roughly doubles retrieval events per unit wall-clock in a four-player game and fixes the dead-time problem that kills co-located turn games on phones.
directives.basis: Corrected: the original proposal replicated the 4-option tap, which lands in the weakest cell of the testing-effect moderator structure (recognition), while cued recall lands in the strongest — at identical interaction cost. Collaborative inhibition also means group retrieval suppresses individual recall, so private simultaneous answering before any reveal is required, not optional: social scoring belongs in the reveal phase, where the re-exposure benefit lives, never in the retrieval phase.

directives.directive: Add a dietaryFlags onboarding step ['pork','shellfish','beef','any-meat','alcohol']; when a flag is set, promote the items that protect it — 肉 猪 蚝油 高汤 荤 素 清真 猪油 火腿 培根 鸡精 — to the front of the queue regardless of tier. This is the one place where ordering should be personalised, because the consequence of a miss is not embarrassment but a meal the player cannot eat. Make 肉 = pork un-skippable for any player who sets a flag, with the hazard-board treatment.
directives.basis: Practitioner-derived but the underlying fact (肉 alone means pork by default; 素 dishes routinely contain 蚝油 or 高汤) is not taught by any HSK level and is verified content.

directives.directive: Keep handwriting entirely off the critical path. The default loop is 100% recognition. If tracing ships at all, make it a single optional finger-trace on FIRST ENCOUNTER only, for a few hundred high-value characters, framed as additive time and never substituted for recognition reps — store traced_at so it never repeats. Do not make stroke-order accuracy a scoring dimension; if anything is scored, score recognisability of the result, not stroke fidelity. Architecturally this means stroke-path data (SVG medians) ships for a few hundred characters, not the whole bank. Ship it behind a flag with per-character (mode, seconds spent, subsequent recognition accuracy at 1 day / 7 days) logging so your own telemetry settles the question for your population — retrofitting per-attempt records with a mode field is expensive.
directives.basis: The recommendation survives regardless of how the handwriting dispute resolves, and it now has an external authority behind it: GF 0025-2021 itself requires 900 reading characters and only 300 handwriting characters at the elementary stage. Character amnesia independently confirms that recognition and production dissociate — even native writers fail production while retaining recognition — which licenses a recognition-only product without apology. State it as a considered trade, not a free choice.

directives.directive: Make the reading-only scope call explicitly and once, and budget it. Either (a) reading-only: cut the sibilant three-way contrast drill, the talker rotation and the pitch-contour pre-test, keep at most one reference audio per item as an optional non-scored affordance, and reclaim the storage for photographs; or (b) reading-plus-listening: keep the audio channel and re-derive the bank size downward to fit the cache budget.
