settled.scope: Cumulative characters → fully decodable words: 300→1,451 (13.1%); 600→3,576 (32.2%); 900→5,801 (52.3%); 1,200→7,330 (66.1%); 1,500→8,358 (75.4%); 1,800→9,361 (84.4%); 3,000→11,086 (99.9%). Level-1's 300 characters cover 100% of level-1's 500 words (not 97.4%). The full 3,000 miss six words, all typographic artefacts: 称¹ 称² 面¹ 面² homograph superscripts and …极了 / …分之… grammar patterns. Character token frequency inside the wordlist: 333 characters for 50%, 1,002 for 80%. 29 of the 3,000 listed characters never appear in any wordlist entry.
sources: Recomputed from GF0025-2021 lists 2026-08-22 — https://github.com/elkmovie/hsk30
settled.implication: Any parser must special-case superscripted homographs, ellipsis pattern entries, ｜-separated alternate forms, 儿-suffixed forms (面条儿 at L1 entry 244) and parenthesised sub-entries (员（服务员） at L3). Build the bank character-first with an explicit dependency graph: every word item stores component_char_ids[]. The motivating progress display is 'you know 312 characters → 1,502 words are now readable', which jumps by tens of words per character landed.

settled.claim: Frequency-ranked running-text coverage, and the size the character spine must actually be.
settled.scope: Computed over jieba's corpus-derived frequency dictionary (349,046 entries, ~100M frequency-weighted hanzi tokens, 12,010 distinct characters), cross-tabulated against GF0025-2021. Frequency-ranked: 300→60.3%, 600→76.8%, 900→85.2%, 1,200→90.0%, 1,500→93.1%, 1,800→95.1%, 2,500→97.6%, 3,000→98.5%; 50% at 195 characters, 90% at 1,198. HSK cumulative sets do worse at equal size: L1's 300 = 43.3% (17 points given away), L1–3's 900 = 79.4%, L1–6's 1,800 = 93.3%, all 3,000 = 97.8%. Dictionary frequencies proxy a balanced written corpus, not signage.
sources: Computed 2026-08-22 over https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fxsjy/jieba/master/jieba/dict.txt, cross-tabulated against https://github.com/elkmovie/hsk30
settled.implication: Size the spine at ~1,500–1,800 characters, not 900. At HSK 1–3's 900 characters roughly one character in five on an unseen sign is still unknown — nowhere near the ~98% conventionally treated as the threshold for unaided reading. Be honest in the UI that 900 characters is 'most of a sign', not 'a sign'.

settled.claim: The HSK-register argument splits by register and is two-thirds wrong as originally stated: menus are a character problem, transit/labels/shopfronts are a compound-parsing problem over characters the learner already nominally knows.
settled.scope: Measured per character against elkmovie/hsk30. Transit (出口 入口 闸机 换乘 末班 首班 站台): 12/12 in HSK 3.0, 10/12 in HSK 1–3 (only 闸 at 7–9 and 乘 at L5 outside). Labels (保质期 净含量 配料 生产日期 冷藏): 13/13 in HSK 3.0, 9/13 in HSK 1–3. Shopfronts (折 满减 特价 现磨): 7/7 and 4/7. Menu: 0/10 cooking verbs in HSK 1–3, with 焗 炝 烩 outside HSK 3.0 entirely; 0/7 ingredients in HSK 1–3, with 笋 藕 韭 outside HSK 3.0. Separately, all 33 'street characters' (乘 促 储 冻 刷 勿 厅 厢 售 巾 扶 招 料 炒 烧 禁 素 腐 荐 藏 袋 询 账 质 购 辣 递 酸 铺 销 闸 馒 鲜) are inside HSK 3,000 (levels 4–7/9) and outside HSK 1–3; 荤 is outside HSK 3,000. Against 通用规范汉字表 (8,105), 笋 藕 韭 菌 are all tier 1; only 焗 炝 烩 煲 fall outside the common 3,500, all in tier 2. The earlier '40% of a 125-item survival set absent from HSK' figure is NOT usable — it counted 儿-suffixed forms, parenthesised sub-entries and transparent N+N compounds (牛肉/猪肉/羊肉/鸡肉, every character in HSK) as absences.
sources: Recomputed 2026-08-22 against https://github.com/elkmovie/hsk30 and https://github.com/jaywcjlove/table-of-general-standard-chinese-characters
settled.implication: Split the v1 bank into two item TYPES, not one 'signage register': character-acquisition items for the menu register, and compound-parsing/cloze items for transit/label/shopfront (换乘, 末班, 净含量, 保质期 are all made of high-frequency characters whose combined meaning is opaque). These need different item formats and different difficulty models.

settled.scope: Headers read on builds 2023-09-03T08:57:17Z (entries=121617) and 2024-12-06T15:50:49Z (entries=122898): 'Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License', https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/, publisher MDBG, ancestor 'CEDICT - Copyright (C) 1997, 1998 Paul Andrew Denisowski'. HONEST SOURCING CAVEAT: both files read were small test fixtures (53 and 31 lines) against a ~123,000-entry distribution — the header is authentic, the read of the full distribution was not performed. settled.implication: Commercial bundling IS permitted. Your derived gloss table IS an adaptation and must ship under BY-SA 4.0; your application code is NOT an adaptation if the dictionary is merely aggregated alongside it. Ship glosses as a separate build artefact (/assets/gloss.cedict.json) with LICENSE-CC-BY-SA-4.0.txt beside it, never inlined into the JS bundle, and publish the derived file in the repo so the obligation is discharged once at build time. DRM TRAP: BY-SA 4.0 §2(a)(5)(B) forbids applying effective technological measures. A PWA on the open web is fine; the same bundle wrapped for the iOS App Store behind FairPlay puts the gloss file's terms in tension with the channel. Stay a PWA, or serve gloss assets as separately-fetched non-DRM'd files.

settled.claim: Unihan / the Unicode Character Database is permissively licensed (MIT-equivalent) and can be bundled in a commercial closed-source PWA with only a notice — but kMandarin must NOT be used for pinyin.
settled.scope: Licence grant: 'use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, and/or sell copies of the Data Files or Software', no fee; condition is that the copyright and permission notice appears with all copies OR in the associated documentation; restriction is that you may not use 'Unicode' or the copyright holder's name in advertising without prior written authorisation. Newer Unicode License v3 is equally permissive. THE FAILURE: kMandarin gives ONE reading per character. 387 of HSK 3.0's 3,000 characters (12.9%) are 多音字; 430 of the common 3,500 (12.3%). A wider count over Unihan readings against 通用规范汉字表 tier 1 gives 1,378 of 3,500 (39.4%) with more than one reading — an upper bound including obsolete literary readings, of which 28.5% differ segmentally and 10.9% by tone alone. kFrequency and kGradeLevel are legacy fields derived from small 1990s sources and are on the deprecated track.

unihan-etl (MIT) tooling — https://github.com/cihai/unihan-etl
settled.implication: Keep Unihan for kTotalStrokes and kRSUnicode — character-intrinsic, single-valued, permissive, and the correct source for the semantic radical (including 肉 → 月, radical 130). Do NOT take pinyin from it: the product's own examples break — 现磨 needs mó not mò, 净含量 needs liàng not liáng, 打折 needs zhé, 菌 is jùn on a menu but jūn by default, 行 is háng in 银行 but xíng in 人行道 and 行李寄存, 便 is biàn in 方便 but pián in 便宜, 地 is dì in 小心地滑 but de as an adverbial marker. Pinyin is a property of the STRING. Take it per-word from CC-CEDICT or hand-author it for a 600–900-string bank. Never order the bank by kFrequency or kGradeLevel without verifying they are still live.

settled.claim: Make Me a Hanzi is dual-licensed and neither half is MIT: dictionary.txt is LGPL-3.0-or-later (derived from Unihan + CJKlib); graphics.txt and svgs.tar.gz are Arphic Public License (derived from AR PL KaitiM GB and AR PL UKai).
settled.scope: makemeahanzi COPYING read verbatim and re-confirmed by an independent reviewer. LGPL on a JSON blob compiled into a Vite bundle is incoherent but not obviously discharged — the mechanism it exists to protect is the right to relink a modified version, which arguably means owing users the ability to swap the file.

skishore/makemeahanzi README (Arphic provenance) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skishore/makemeahanzi/master/README.md
settled.implication: Do not ship dictionary.txt, in any form, in any column. Regenerate the equivalent decomposition and radical data from Unihan (permissive) plus CC-CEDICT (BY-SA), which is where most of it came from anyway. Enforce it with a build-time provenance manifest (column → dataset → licence) and fail CI on any column with no entry and on any field traceable to dictionary.txt. Ten lines of script; it is the difference between a defensible product and an undocumented one.

settled.claim: Arphic Public License exact terms: it permits commercial sale and bundling, but it is genuinely copyleft on the stroke data and imposes a 'designated place' distribution duty on modifications.
settled.scope: Full APL text read verbatim, twice, including as shipped inside hanzi-writer-data@2.0.1. §1 permits verbatim redistribution without restriction; the 'Freely Available' definition says 'If you wish, you can charge for this service'. ARPHICPL.TXT must be retained unaltered in all copies. §2(a) requires a prominent notice in each modified file stating how and when you changed it. §2(b) requires modifications be made Freely Available as a whole to all third parties under the same licence, 'such as by offering access to copy the modifications from a designated place'. §2 carries an explicit mere-aggregation carve-out — that is what actually protects your app code. §0 contemplates renaming the font. §3 auto-terminates on non-compliance. §5 bars imposing further restrictions on recipients — the same DRM tension as CC BY-SA. FSF lists the APL as free but GPL-incompatible. Converting the SVG outlines to a different JSON shape, or re-subsetting to your character set, IS a modification and triggers §2(a) and §2(b). hanzi-writer-data declares "license": "SEE LICENSE IN ARPHICPL.TXT" and ships ARPHICPL.TXT plus an APL/ directory with five localised copies; the hanzi-writer CODE is MIT.
sources: Arphic Public License full text, as vendored — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rougier/freetype-gl/master/fonts/fireflysung-LICENSE.txt and as shipped in hanzi-writer-data@2.0.1
chanind/hanzi-writer-data — https://github.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data
chanind/hanzi-writer (MIT code) — https://github.com/chanind/hanzi-writer
settled.implication: If you ever ship stroke graphics, publish your reformatted subset as a public GitHub repo under the APL with ARPHICPL.TXT and a CHANGES file — that one repo is the 'designated place' and discharges the whole obligation permanently. But see the next finding: for v1 you should not ship them at all.

settled.claim: Stroke-order graphics are both the wrong data for a reading game and the most expensive asset available — measured, they are about a third larger than commonly assumed.
settled.scope: Measured across the whole of hanzi-writer-data@2.0.1: 9,574 per-character JSON files, mean 3,368 B, median 3,273 B, range 217–8,621 B. A 3,000-character bank is 9.64 MB raw, ≈3.9 MB gzip -9, ≈3.1 MB brotli q11; a 1,200-character bank is 3.85 MB raw / 1.53 MB gzip / 1.21 MB brotli (41% / 32% of raw). Structure is {strokes: SVG paths, medians: polylines, radStrokes: indices}. Separately: stroke ORDER as an ordered integer sequence (standardised by the PRC GB 现代汉语通用字笔顺规范) is a fact/standard, not an expressive work, and carries far less copyright risk than the Arphic-derived outlines. KanjiVG (CC BY-SA 3.0) is the other free option but is Japanese-centric and misses simplified-only forms.
sources: Measured 2026-08-22: npm pack hanzi-writer-data@2.0.1, per-file sizes over 9,574 JSON files, gzip level 9 and brotli quality 11 over a seeded 1,200-file concatenation
chanind/hanzi-writer-data — https://github.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data
settled.implication: Ship NO stroke graphics in v1. At 1.21 MB brotli even a 1,200-character stroke bundle alone would consume 40% of a 3 MB install budget, for a skill this product's user will never perform, plus an APL copyleft obligation. If a 'how is this written' affordance is wanted later, lazy-load the single character's JSON on demand from a separate APL-licensed static path — never in the install payload of an offline-first PWA. If you only need order, ship the integer sequence.

settled.claim: HSK list copyright is genuinely unsettled and is routinely misreported in both directions; the real exposure is trademark, not copyright.
settled.scope: The underlying source is 《国际中文教育中文水平等级标准》 GF 0025-2021, a PRC national standard issued by MOE/CLEC. PRC Copyright Law Art. 5 excludes laws, regulations and official documents of state organs from protection, but national standards (GB/GF) sit in a contested category where SAC and issuing ministries assert rights. Independently, a bare word list is a compilation of facts with thin originality in most jurisdictions. elkmovie/hsk30 carries '# Copyright (c) 2021 Pleco Inc. # Distributed under MIT license' — Pleco's grant covers Pleco's OCR and compilation labour only and cannot grant rights MOE might hold. Announcement URL is .../s5987/202103/t20210329_523304.html (March 2021); the .../202104/t20210401_523302.html figure that circulates is wrong. Neither was retrievable.
sources: elkmovie/hsk30, MIT, Pleco Inc. 2021 — https://github.com/elkmovie/hsk30
MOE announcement of GF 0025-2021 (unretrieved) — http://www.moe.gov.cn/jyb_xwfb/gzdt_gzdt/s5987/202103/t20210329_523304.html
settled.implication: Use elkmovie/hsk30 as an internal difficulty-ordering signal only, and attribute Pleco + MIT in /licences. Never use the letters 'HSK', the HSK logo, or 'HSK Level N' as a user-facing label or in store metadata — that is the exposure that actually bites. Store hsk_band as an integer 1–9 internally and label the player-facing bands with your own vocabulary.

settled.claim: 通用规范汉字表 (Table of General Standard Chinese Characters, GF 0023-2013) is a strictly better character spine than HSK, and an MIT-licensed machine-readable copy exists that also solves the heteronym and traditional-variant problems.
settled.scope: Cloned and analysed: data/characters.json = 8,105 characters in the three official tiers (3,500 / 3,000 / 1,605); data/pinyin.duo.json = 597 多音字 with all readings; data/simplified.convert.json = 1,489 simplified→traditional with 1:many arrays; data/traditional.convert.json = 1,520; data/pinyin.json per-character readings. Cross-check: HSK 3.0's 3,000 characters are 98.9% inside TGH tier 1 (2,967), 33 in tier 2, 0 outside TGH. TGH strictly contains HSK and adds the ~500 tier-1 characters HSK omits — exactly where the missing signage characters live (笋 藕 韭 are TGH tier 1 and absent from HSK 3.0). SAME LEGAL CAVEAT as HSK: GF 0023-2013 is a PRC national standard; a third party's MIT grant covers their transcription labour only.
sources: jaywcjlove/table-of-general-standard-chinese-characters, MIT, cloned and analysed 2026-08-22 — https://github.com/jaywcjlove/table-of-general-standard-chinese-characters
settled.implication: Use TGH tier as the difficulty spine and HSK band as a secondary signal — which also reduces your dependence on the HSK trademark. Take the 597-entry 多音字 table directly; it is the fastest fix for the pinyin-correctness problem. Take the 1:many traditional tables as a HAZARD LIST, not a converter.

settled.claim: Simplified versus traditional is a hard fork in the item bank that cannot be papered over with a conversion step, and the one-to-many cases cluster in exactly the survival/menu vocabulary this product targets.
settled.scope: Computed by joining OpenCC's STCharacters.txt against the GF0025-2021 3,000-character reading list: 1,790 identical in traditional, 980 with exactly one different traditional form, 230 mapping to MORE THAN ONE traditional character — 89 of those 230 fall inside the first 900 characters. Verified 1:many: 面 → 麵/麪 (noodles) vs 面 (face/surface); 干 → 乾/幹/干/榦 (乾 on every 乾拌/乾貨 label); 发 → 發/髮; 后 → 後/后; 里 → 裏/里/哩; 表 → 表/錶; 系 → 系/係/繫; 只 → 只/隻; 台 → 臺/檯/颱; 历 → 歷/曆; 钟 → 鐘/鍾; 复 → 復/複; 尽 → 盡/儘; 板 → 闆; 松 → 鬆; 斗 → 鬥. OpenCC's own phrase table renders 面条 as 麪條 and 收银台 as 收銀臺. Regional lexis diverges independently of script (mainland 换乘/单程票/充值 vs Taiwan usage), so 'convert on export' produces text no one has ever seen on a sign. Separately, PRC language law permits 繁体字 in enumerated cases including 题词和招牌的手书字 — calligraphic shop signage — so shopfront fascias are the one domain where traditional forms routinely appear (理发 vs 理髮, 面馆 vs 麵館/麪館).
sources: Computed 2026-08-22 by joining https://github.com/BYVoid/OpenCC STCharacters.txt against https://github.com/elkmovie/hsk30
simplified→traditional 1:many mappings, data/simplified.convert.json (1,489 entries) — https://github.com/jaywcjlove/table-of-general-standard-chinese-characters
《中华人民共和国国家通用语言文字法》 (2000) Art. 17 — cited from record, gov.cn 403-blocked; verify before quoting
settled.implication: Three consequences the architecture cannot absorb late: (1) the character-dependency graph is not isomorphic across scripts, so component_char_ids[] must be script-scoped, never shared; (2) per-character FSRS state does not transfer — 面 and 麪 are two retrieval targets; (3) never auto-convert — picking 幹 instead of 乾 for 干 (on every Sichuan menu: 干煸, 干锅, 豆干) yields a character that reads as an expletive in Taiwanese usage. Ship simplified only in v1, store trad as a LIST per string, and CI-fail on any item containing 面/干/发/后/里/松/只/几/表/系/术 with a scalar trad field.

settled.claim: All three commonly-bundled Chinese frequency lists have licence problems, none of them measures signage, and they disagree with each other by ~5–6 points at rank 1,000.
settled.scope: SUBTLEX-CH (Cai & Brysbaert 2010, PLoS ONE 5(6):e10729): the data file header was read this session and confirms 'Total character count: 46,841,097', 'Total word count: 33,546,516', 'Context number: 6,243'. Licence UNVERIFIED — PLoS ONE articles are CC BY and the tables were Supporting Information, so the SI copy is the safe one; the lab-site and GitHub mirrors carry no licence text (leonsilicon/subtlex-ch-wf states none), which is itself the warning. Jun Da's MTSU list: free for research and teaching, no open licence, no commercial grant — and bundled commercially all over the ecosystem regardless. BCC (~15bn characters) is a query service; the circulating global_wordfreq.release.txt has no licence statement. DISAGREEMENT MEASURED: cumulative coverage at rank 1,000 is 93.97% on SUBTLEX-CH versus 87.1% on a jieba-derived curve; two corpora both called 'Chinese character frequency' do not even agree on their top three.

Unencumbered alternatives that are verified: Unihan kFrequency (coarse 1–5 buckets, but legacy), Common Voice sentence text (CC0), Chinese Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0).

settled.claim: A published, downloadable, character-level frequency corpus of Chinese text in the urban wild already exists — but its annotations are NON-COMMERCIAL.
settled.scope: CTW (Chinese Text in the Wild), Tsinghua University / Tencent Joint Laboratory: 32,285 high-resolution street-view images, 1,018,402 individually character-labelled instances, 3,850 distinct character categories, each instance with a polygon and six attributes (occluded, bgcomplex, distorted, raised, wordart, handwritten). LICENCE: annotations CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, baseline code MIT. The shipped baseline even has a STAT_FREQUENCY = 'products/stat_frequency.json' build step. Verified first-party from the project homepage source and repository. Corroborating: RCTW-17 (12,263 images), ICDAR 2019 ReCTS (~25k SIGNBOARD images). BIAS: Tencent street-view imagery over-represents shopfront fascias and street signage and under-represents menus, shelf-edge labels and indoor plates — the three highest-payoff domains.
sources: Yuan, T.-L., Zhu, Z., Xu, K., Li, C.-J., Mu, T.-J. & Hu, S.-M. (2019), A Large Chinese Text Dataset in the Wild, J. Computer Science and Technology 34(3), 509–521 — https://ctwdataset.github.io/
ctw-baseline (character-level annotation format; judge/settings.py STAT_FREQUENCY) — https://github.com/yuantailing/ctw-baseline
settled.implication: Compute the signage frequency distribution from CTW in an afternoon instead of photographing Beijing — BUT the NC term is a real gate on a commercial product and must be resolved before a derived frequency table enters the bundle. Two routes: (a) obtain a commercial grant from the authors, or (b) use CTW internally only, as a research input that informs which characters you author, and ship no artefact derived from the annotations. Route (b) is defensible and free. Either way, the 'we photographed 200 menus and own a dataset nobody has' claim is dead: 5,000 captures is a rounding error against 1,018,402 labelled instances.

settled.claim: There is no shippable open Mandarin audio source for this product, and the corpus licences behind 'open source' Chinese TTS are the trap.
settled.scope: VERIFIED: Mozilla Common Voice sentence text is CC0, the repository is MPL 2.0; Mandarin locales zh-CN, zh-TW, zh-HK. But CV clips are whole read sentences by volunteers of highly variable quality with no forced alignment shipped — extracting a clean single-word pronunciation is a research project, not a build step. Forvo is a proprietary paid API whose terms forbid redistribution and durable caching of the audio — structurally incompatible with an offline PWA. PRIOR KNOWLEDGE, VERIFY BEFORE USE: AISHELL-3 Apache-2.0; THCHS-30 Apache-2.0; MagicData Mandarin CC BY-ND 4.0 (ND arguably prohibits training a model on it); CSMSC / 标贝 explicitly NON-COMMERCIAL and the default single-speaker corpus behind a large fraction of publicly released Chinese TTS checkpoints. Web Speech API: the zh-CN voice is frequently absent on iOS Safari and synthesis requires a user gesture.
sources: common-voice/common-voice README — dataset CC0, code MPL 2.0 — https://github.com/common-voice/common-voice
Common Voice datasets page — INACCESSIBLE THIS SESSION — https://commonvoice.mozilla.org/en/datasets
settled.implication: Ship NO audio in v1 — this is a reading game and audio is a multi-megabyte tax on a skill the product does not claim. When it is added: pre-render at build time for the finite bank using a commercial TTS whose terms grant output rights (Azure, Google, ElevenLabs all do), ship Opus at 24 kbps mono (~900 items × 1.5 s ≈ 4 MB) in Cache Storage with per-item eviction, and never rely on the Web Speech API — it fails exactly at a table with mixed phones.

settled.claim: Noto Sans SC and Source Han Sans are the same typeface under two licences, and only one of them is safe to subset: Source Han Sans carries the Reserved Font Name 'Source'; Noto CJK declares no RFN at all.
settled.scope: Both licence files read verbatim and independently re-confirmed. Source Han Sans LICENSE.txt: SIL OFL 1.1, 26 February 2007, 'Copyright 2014-2025 Adobe … with Reserved Font Name Source', which is also an Adobe trademark. notofonts/noto-cjk Sans/LICENSE: OFL 1.1, no copyright line and no RFN. OFL obligations that apply: you may bundle, embed, modify and sell-with-software at no cost; you must include the copyright notice and the licence with the font; the modified font stays under OFL 1.1; the font may not be sold on its own. SUBSETTING COUNTS AS MODIFICATION.

adobe-fonts/source-han-sans LICENSE.txt, OFL 1.1 with RFN 'Source' — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adobe-fonts/source-han-sans/release/LICENSE.txt
settled.implication: Use Noto Sans SC, not Source Han Sans, precisely because it carries no RFN. Give the subset a distinct internal family name so no trademark or RFN question can arise. Ship OFL.txt alongside it and list it in /licences.

settled.claim: The CJK font sizes everyone quotes are wrong by 4–5x, and the tofu risk everyone fears is created by your own subsetting step, not by the typeface. All measured with fonttools/pyftsubset.
settled.scope: @fontsource/noto-sans-sc@5.3.0 ships BOTH ~97 numbered unicode-range chunks per weight (2.27 MB total at w400, mean 24 KB each — and this is what the DEFAULT index.css uses) AND five named subsets. The named chinese-simplified woff2 @400 = 1,142,552 B = 1.09 MB, containing 7,946 codepoints / 7,333 CJK ideographs / 8,248 glyphs — not 4–5 MB and not ~44k glyphs. Separately measured from notofonts/noto-cjk: NotoSansSC-Regular.otf = 7.95 MB; NotoSansSC-VF.otf = 15.05 MB. pyftsubset 4.63.0 (woff2, --layout-features= stripped, --no-hinting, plus 121 Latin/punctuation codepoints): 300 hanzi → 44.7 KB; 600 → 84.9 KB; 900 → 123.5 KB; 1,200 → 164.0 KB; 2,000 → 277.4 KB; 3,000 → 418.6 KB — near-linear at 109–137 bytes/glyph. An independent 482-glyph subset (378 CJK + Latin + digits + tone-marked vowels + punctuation) measured 60.0 KB woff2 / 66.3 KB woff. COVERAGE VERIFIED: the chinese-simplified subset contains all 3,000 HSK 3.0 characters and all of 焗 煲 涮 菌 藕 韭 笋 蒜 姜 葱 炝 烩 氽 煨 熘 腌 蕈 蚝 蛏 鲈 鳕 鳝 — tofu risk from the typeface is zero.

KonghaYao/cn-font-split, Apache-2.0 — https://github.com/KonghaYao/cn-font-split

settled.claim: Google Fonts' CSS API is disqualified twice over for this product: it requires network at render time, and its hosts are unreachable from mainland China.
settled.scope: The packaging half is verified (CJK is served as ~100 lazily-fetched unicode-range chunks, which cannot be service-worker precached coherently). The China-blocking half is widely documented but NOT independently verifiable from this sandbox — the egress proxy reaches fonts.googleapis.com, which says nothing about conditions inside China. The engineering fix is correct regardless of the answer.

Google Fonts host blocking in mainland China — verify from a mainland vantage point before ship
